MEMORANDUM

TO: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel
FROM: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
DATE: April 5, 2023
SUBJECT: Litigation Reserve Recommendation — ApexHip Product Liability (Q2 2023)

Rob, Rachel:

Following our preliminary review of Q1 close figures and in light of external developments over the past six weeks, Finance recommends an immediate adjustment to the product liability reserve established for ApexHip. Specifically, we recommend increasing the existing $18.0M accrual established in Q3 2022 by $8.0M, bringing the total litigation reserve to $26.0M effective for the Q2 2023 financial statements.

Basis for Reserve Adjustment

As discussed with Whitfield & Barr last month, the service of the initial state-court complaints in late March represents a formal transition from an unasserted potential liability to active litigation. The underlying clinical exposure cited in these initial filings tracks precisely with the registry data we reviewed internally throughout 2021:

1. NJR 7.1% 5-Year Revision Rate: The initial complaints heavily quote the March 2021 NJR annual report benchmark (7.1% vs. 3.2% class average) as prima facie evidence of elevated failure.
2. AJRR Corroboration: Late-2021 AJRR registry metrics, which demonstrated parallel divergence in domestic revision curves, have now been incorporated into plaintiff filings regarding ARMD and elevated cobalt/chromium ion levels.

Given the rate of initial filings and discussions with outside counsel regarding potential consolidation scenarios, Hannah Berg and I modeled defense costs, potential initial settlement valuations, and retention liabilities under our Aegis Specialty policy. As you know, Aegis issued a reservation of rights last year, meaning defense expense erosion will fall heavily within our direct retention before excess coverage responds. An accrual of $26.0M aligns more closely with probable and reasonably estimable losses under ASC 450.

Commercial Impact & Top-Line Drag

The legal exposure continues to compound top-line erosion. The commercial fallout from the registry disclosures, the October 2021 surgeon notification, and the residual confusion from the unrelated 2022 cup coating recall has severely impaired Apex reorder rates.

Hannah’s FP&A team has completed the updated spring forecast. ApexHip annualized revenue for FY2023 has been revised downward again, dropping from our prior budget projection of $54M to approximately $42.0M annualized. This represents a significant contraction from peak 2020 revenue ($96M) and will create an operational margin drag of roughly 180 bps across Reconstructive.

Please let me know when we can take 15 minutes to align before I brief the Audit Committee ahead of the May board meeting.

Re: 510(k) Submission K162447 — ApexHip Total Hip System

Dear Dr. Anand:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. respectfully submits this premarket notification pursuant to Section 510(k) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for the ApexHip Total Hip System.

ApexHip is indicated for total hip arthroplasty in skeletally mature patients, including active adults ages 45 through 65, where the treating surgeon determines that a metal-on-metal total hip system is clinically appropriate. The system consists of a cobalt-chromium (Co/Cr) femoral stem and femoral head, and a Co/Cr acetabular cup incorporating Veridian’s KinetiCoat porous titanium coating to support biological fixation.

The predicate device is Veridian’s legally marketed ClassicHip Total Hip System. ApexHip has the same general intended use and fundamental scientific technology as the predicate: replacement of the natural hip joint with implanted femoral and acetabular components. The submission provides a comparison of device design, materials, dimensional ranges, sterilization, packaging, labeling, and performance characteristics. Differences in component configuration and the KinetiCoat porous titanium surface are addressed through the enclosed bench, materials, and biocompatibility evaluations.

Wear testing was conducted in accordance with the ISO 14242 protocol approved during Design Review DR-3. The testing supports that the device performs as intended under the specified test conditions and that the identified design differences do not raise new questions of safety or effectiveness.

Veridian has substantial prior experience with the predicate device family and related hip reconstruction systems. In light of that clearance history and the complete performance information provided, we respectfully request an expedited review of this submission where feasible.

Please direct any questions or requests for additional information to my attention at (574) 555-0148 or dokonkwo@veridianortho.com.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs

REGULATORY AFFAIRS INTERNAL MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
FROM: Devon Mitchell, Sr. Regulatory Specialist
DATE: July 8, 2022
SUBJECT: Cumulative MDR Count & Trending Summary: ApexHip Metal-Ion / ARMD Events (Mid-Year 2022)

Purpose
This memorandum provides an updated mid-year 2022 reconciliation of cumulative Medical Device Reports (MDRs) submitted to FDA CDRH under 21 CFR Part 803 concerning the ApexHip Total Hip System, specifically focusing on reports alleging elevated cobalt/chromium (Co/Cr) ion levels, adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR), pseudotumors, or adverse reactions to metal debris (ARMD).

Cumulative Submission Metrics (2018 – H1 2022)
Since the first tracked cluster originating out of the Southeast region in August 2018, Veridian has submitted a total of thirty-four (34) individual MDRs associated with metal-ion release and/or ARMD leading to revision or surgical intervention.

The annual distribution of these filings is summarized below:

* 2018: 3 MDRs (initial cluster originating from Dr. Feld's practice; TrackWise ref TW-2018-0882 series)
* 2019: 5 MDRs
* 2020: 7 MDRs
* 2021: 10 MDRs
* 2022 (H1, Jan 1 – Jun 30): 9 MDRs
* Cumulative Total: 34 MDRs

The filing velocity has accelerated notably over the past eighteen months, with H1 2022 alone accounting for over 26% of our total historical MDR submissions for this failure mode.

Reporting Timeliness & Compliance
A review of submission timelines confirms that all thirty-four filings were submitted within the statutory 30-day reporting window, with the exception of two late submissions identified during Q1 2019. Those two occurrences were self-identified, logged under internal CAPA, and formally remediated and closed following our updated intake escalation procedure. All nine submissions generated in H1 2022 met 30-day compliance requirements from initial date of awareness in TrackWise.

Regulatory Context & FDA Interaction
Following our submission of the formal Additional Information (AI) response to FDA CDRH in May 2019 regarding metal-ion complaint trending, the agency has not issued any subsequent formal AI requests or inquiries specific to ApexHip MoM wear performance or ion generation. Furthermore, while the June 2021 FDA inspection of Warsaw resulted in a Form 483 observation regarding general complaint trending timeliness, our July 2021 response adequately addressed the procedural remediation.

However, given ongoing registry-driven scrutiny—including the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) 5-year revision metrics and similar signal trends in AJRR data—our continuing increase in domestic filing velocity represents a significant regulatory exposure. While the current voluntary Class II recall (Z-1418-2022) remains strictly limited to coating adhesion issues on Cork cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, the steady uptick in ARMD-related MDRs could readily prompt CDRH/Office of Compliance to reopen inquiry into overall system wear performance.

We will continue monthly reconciliations with Quality and Post-Market Surveillance.

cc: Priya Raman, Director of Quality & Complaint Handling

MEMORANDUM

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL // PREPARED AT THE DIRECTION OF LEGAL COUNSEL

TO: Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel; Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
FROM: Hannah Berg, FP&A Manager
DATE: September 28, 2022
SUBJECT: Reserve Methodology Summary — Response to Aegis Inquiry

Executive Summary

In response to coverage counsel's inquiry from Aegis Specialty regarding the $18.0M reserve recorded in Q3 2022 for ApexHip product liability exposure, this memorandum outlines the underlying quantitative framework, population baselines, and actuarial cost assumptions.

The $18.0M accrued figure reflects a probabilistic expected-loss model that evaluates exposure across two distinct tranches: (1) baseline product liability arising from the June 2022 Class II recall (coating adhesion defect), and (2) anticipated broader metal-on-metal (MoM) revision and adverse local tissue reaction exposure (potential MDL cluster).

1. Population Baselines & Claim Frequency Modeling

The reserve calculation models frequency across two discrete cohorts:

*   Cohort A (Direct Recall Population): Pertains specifically to cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 (Z-1418-2022). Of the 1,140 units distributed, tracing records confirmed 412 units implanted. Given the visible nature of intraoperative flaking and post-market tracking, we applied an initial claim conversion rate of 25%–35% across the 412 patients, establishing an estimated 100 to 145 discrete claims directly linked to the manufacturing issue.
*   Cohort B (Broader MoM / Registry-Informed Exposure): To establish incremental exposure for broader revision claims likely to seek consolidation, the model incorporates external registry benchmarks. Specifically, we utilized the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 5-year cumulative revision rate for ApexHip of 7.1%, set against the MoM class average benchmark of 3.2%. The 3.9% differential ("excess revision delta") was applied to the cumulative implanted US ApexHip population from launch through year-end 2021 (~31,500 total systems). Applying an estimated legal capture rate of 15%–20% to that excess revision population yields an incremental claim projection of 185 to 245 claims developing across a 24–36 month horizon.

2. Severity and Cost Benchmarks

Per-claim indemnity and defense costs were benchmarked against historical orthopedic MDL and state-court MoM mass-tort settlements over the 2012–2019 period (adjusting for inflation and current defense cost trajectories):

*   Average Indemnity per Revised Implant: Modeled at $85,000–$110,000 net settlement value per revised claimant presenting documented ARMD/tissue necrosis or confirmed coating delamination.
*   Defense & Case Processing Cost: Modeled at an average of $22,000 per filed matter through early resolution or bellwether discovery.
*   Total Blended Cost per Actionable Claim: Estimated at approximately $115,000 across unrepresented and represented claims.

3. Conclusion & Reserve Appropriateness

Applying these parameters across both cohorts generates an un-discounted nominal exposure range of $16.2M (low-end estimate) to $22.8M (high-end stress estimate).

$$\text{Midpoint Expected Loss} \approx \$18.15\text{M}$$

Accordingly, the FP&A team determined that the booked $18.0M reserve remains appropriate and defensible under ASC 450 as a best estimate within the range pending further claim maturation. We recommend providing Aegis with the broad methodology structure outlined above while withholding internal sensitivity tables.

Date: Thu, 08 Sep 2022 14:22:15 -0400
Subject: Draft MDR Trend Summary for FDA Follow-Up

Dana,

Per our discussion following the informal inquiry from CDRH last week regarding the post-recall monitoring under Z-1418-2022, I have put together the preliminary draft of the complaint and MDR trending data for ApexHip through August 31.

The draft covers both failure modes currently logged in TrackWise:

1. KinetiCoat Adhesion / Delamination: Specific to the Cork plasma-spray parameter drift affecting cup lots V-2200 through V-2299. We have 14 confirmed incoming inspection reports and 6 intraoperative/unwrapping reports captured under CAPA-2022-004. These numbers have flattened considerably since the recall communication went out in June.

2. ARMD / Metal-on-Metal Wear / Early Revision: Ongoing post-market reporting reflecting elevated cobalt/chromium ion levels, pain, tissue necrosis, and revisions (predominantly cups larger than 52 mm, often tracking with high inclination). We have 28 new complaints logged in Q2 alone, with 19 progressing to MDR filings.

My main concern with the current roll-up is visual and contextual presentation. In the draft document (attached as `Apex_MDR_Trending_Q2_2022_Draft.pdf`), Devon had combined these into a single monthly ApexHip adverse event trending chart.

In my view, combining the coating adhesion failures with the metal-ion/revision complaints in one overarching trend line is going to create confusion for the reviewer. The root causes and clinical presentations are entirely distinct—one is a contained manufacturing issue under active recall, while the other reflects clinical wear performance and registry-aligned signals.

Should we present these as two clearly separated charts in the response packet to ensure the agency does not conflate the two populations, or do you prefer keeping the single aggregate curve per standard trending SOP?

Regards,

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

For ApexHip, we have 47 complaints since launch, of which 12 reference pain with elevated Co/Cr values where a value was provided, 9 reference a revision or planned revision, and 6 include both. The Atlanta cases are:
- TW-2018-0341
- TW-2018-0355
- TW-2018-0362

Those were escalated at intake, evaluated for MDR reportability, and handled under the applicable complaint procedure. The three reports came from the same practice and were appropriately reviewed as a cluster; that does not establish a product-wide trend. Since February, we have received four similar allegations, including two outside Georgia. The individual reportability determinations are in the attached worksheet.

I understand FDA is asking about the proposed design change. From Quality’s perspective, ECO-2019-118 remains deferred pending completion of the engineering evaluation; it is not a CAPA and does not alter the adequacy of the complaint handling performed to date.

Please let me know if you need the geography breakout reformatted for the response.

Priya

Re: Notification of Voluntary Market Withdrawal – ApexHip Total Hip System

To Whom It May Concern:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. is providing notice that it intends to voluntarily withdraw the ApexHip Total Hip System from the United States market effective February 2, 2024.

ApexHip is a metal-on-metal total hip system cleared under 510(k) K162447 on March 9, 2017. The product includes cobalt/chromium femoral components and a cobalt/chromium acetabular cup with KinetiCoat porous titanium coating. Veridian will cease U.S. commercial distribution of ApexHip on the effective date and will communicate the withdrawal to affected customers, distributors, and surgeon users.

This action follows Veridian’s assessment of the totality of available post-market information regarding the system’s metal-ion and wear performance profile. That assessment includes the UK National Joint Registry annual report issued in March 2021, which identified a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1 percent compared with a 3.2 percent class average, as well as subsequent American Joint Replacement Registry trends that raised similar concerns. Veridian has also considered clinical complaint information, including reports involving elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels, adverse reaction to metal debris, and early revision procedures.

In addition, Veridian is aware that multidistrict litigation concerning ApexHip was formed in December 2023. While the litigation is ongoing and no conclusions should be drawn from this notice regarding any particular allegation or claim, its formation is among the circumstances considered in Veridian’s decision to discontinue commercial availability of the system.

This voluntary market withdrawal is separate from Veridian’s June 14, 2022 voluntary Class II recall of certain ApexHip acetabular cup lots, V-2200 through V-2299, under FDA Recall Number Z-1418-2022. That recall addressed a manufacturing-related KinetiCoat adhesion issue associated with plasma-spray parameter drift at the Cork facility. The present withdrawal does not concern that coating issue. Rather, it addresses the distinct metal-ion/wear performance profile identified through registry, complaint, and other post-market data.

Veridian does not recommend prophylactic revision solely as a result of this market withdrawal. Patients with implanted ApexHip systems should continue routine clinical follow-up as determined by their treating surgeon, including evaluation and monitoring based on the patient’s symptoms, clinical presentation, and surgeon judgment. Veridian will continue to meet its complaint handling, medical device reporting, and other post-market surveillance obligations under applicable requirements, including 21 CFR Parts 803 and 820.

Please direct any questions regarding this notification to my attention at (574) 555-0142 or dokonkwo@veridianortho.com.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Regulatory Affairs Memorandum

Date: November 15, 2022
From: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
Subject: Recall Closure Memorandum - Z-1418-2022, ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299

This memorandum documents final reconciliation and recommended closure of Veridian Orthopedics’ voluntary Class II recall of ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 (FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022).

The recall was initiated on June 14, 2022, following reports from two hospital incoming-inspection locations of KinetiCoat coating flaking on cups removed from their sterile packaging. The affected lots were manufactured at the Cork facility between November 2021 and February 2022. The field action applied only to the identified acetabular cup lots and was not associated with post-market reports concerning metal ion levels, wear, or ARMD.

Final distribution reconciliation is as follows:

| Disposition | Units |
|---|---:|
| Total units distributed | 1,140 |
| Confirmed implanted before recall notification | 412 |
| Returned to Veridian / distributor inventory | 681 |
| Customer-destroyed with documentation received | 47 |
| Total recovered or otherwise accounted for | 728 |

All 1,140 distributed units have now been reconciled through documented implantation status, return, or customer-certified destruction. Recall effectiveness checks, including follow-up to non-responding accounts and distributor verification, reached a final effectiveness rate of 98.6% after reconciliation. The remaining 1.4% represents accounts for which receipt of the recall communication was confirmed through alternate records, including shipment, email delivery, and distributor contact documentation, but a completed response form was not obtained despite repeated follow-up.

The investigation concluded that the coating adhesion condition resulted from plasma-spray parameter drift following an October 2021 chamber maintenance event at the Cork facility. Specifically, the chamber was returned to production without adequate confirmation that operating parameters remained within validated ranges for application of the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating. Batch records and retained-sample review supported the conclusion that the issue was limited to the affected lot range.

Corrective and preventive actions were managed under CAPA-2022-0091. Actions included recertification of Chamber 3, revalidation of the applicable plasma-spray operating window, enhanced verification following maintenance activity, revised maintenance-release documentation, and tightened process-control review requirements for coating runs. Quality has verified implementation and effectiveness of these actions. CAPA-2022-0091 is now closed.

Regulatory Affairs recommends that the FDA District Office be notified that recall effectiveness activities and final reconciliation are complete, with closure requested for Recall No. Z-1418-2022. Recall records, including customer notifications, response records, distribution and return reconciliation, investigation materials, CAPA documentation, and FDA correspondence, should be retained in accordance with 21 CFR 806.20. The DHF-linked recall file should be archived in Agile with cross-references to the Cork manufacturing investigation and CAPA-2022-0091.

Dana

MEMORANDUM

TO: Marketing Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Product Management (ApexHip)
FROM: Anika Shah, Director, Marketing Communications
DATE: July 1, 2019
SUBJECT: Q2 2019 Claim Substantiation File Update – ApexHip™ System

1. Purpose & Scope
In accordance with SOP-MKT-042 (Promotional Review and Claim Substantiation), this memorandum documents the quarterly verification of active claims, supporting substantiation packages, and collateral status for the ApexHip Total Hip System. All marketing literature, digital assets, and field collateral currently in circulation must map directly to validated design inputs, clinical literature, or bench testing on file.

2. Q2 Collateral Sign-Offs & Routine Inventory Re-Orders
During the second quarter of 2019, MarCom conducted review cycles on several high-volume sales enablement assets. The following materials were processed and approved for reprint or digital distribution:
*   *ApexHip Surgical Technique Guide (Lit. No. ML-APX-002, Rev. C)*: Routine formatting corrections; updated diagram callouts for primary cup impactor positioning. No claim alterations.
*   *ApexHip Patient Education Brochure (Lit. No. PE-APX-014, Rev. B)*: Re-order run of 5,000 units with Kessler Reid. Retains the "Active Life" positioning pillars approved in 2017.
*   *ApexHip System Sell Sheet (Lit. No. SS-APX-008, Rev. D)*: Updated regional distributor contact information for Southwest and Mid-Atlantic sales zones.

No substantive claim additions, headline changes, or modified comparative statements were introduced in these releases.

3. Existing Core Claims Reaffirmation
The established promotional claims for ApexHip remain substantiated under Design History File DHF-0042 and 510(k) K162447 clearance documentation:
*   *Claim 1*: "Designed for stability and reduced dislocation risk through optimized anatomical head-to-neck ratios across large-diameter Co/Cr head offerings (36–50 mm)." (Substantiated via Meridian Testing Labs kinematic range-of-motion modeling, Report TR-16-088).
*   *Claim 2*: "KinetiCoat porous titanium plasma-spray promotes biological fixation and immediate scratch fit." (Substantiated via KBT acquisition bench test data and push-out shear testing, DHF-0042, Sec. 4.3).
*   *Claim 3*: "Engineered for low volumetric wear in high-demand, active adult patient demographics." (Substantiated via ISO 14242-1 standard gait simulator wear testing at 45° nominal cup inclination, Report MTL-2016-0412).

4. Forward-Looking Watch Items & Guidance
*Wear Simulation & Durability Messaging:* MarCom has been briefed by Tom Halvorsen’s R&D engineering group regarding ongoing follow-up simulator evaluations. Engineering is currently re-running wear testing protocols evaluated at steeper, higher inclination angles beyond nominal ISO parameters. Depending on the final simulator outputs, these findings could affect future durability and long-term bearing wear messaging for the cup system.

Consequently, effective immediately, marketing and commercial teams must not introduce any new durability, wear rate, or implant longevity claims across any promotional channels until Halvorsen's engineering analysis and full cross-functional review are finalized. MarCom will maintain this as an open watch item heading into the Q3 2019 claim review cycle.

cc: Carlos Mendes, Dana Okonkwo, Priya Raman

I met with Tom on August 11 as part of the informal mid-year check-in cycle for the ApexHip engineering group. This was not a formal performance review and no action is required in Workday at this time.

Tom continues to perform strongly in his Senior Design Engineer role. His technical knowledge of the Apex system, including historical design decisions, wear-testing methodology, and supporting DHF documentation, remains unusually deep. His manager reports that he is responsive on technical questions, thorough with data review, and dependable when cross-functional teams need historical context. Tom has also been helpful to newer engineers who are trying to understand the legacy KBT coating work and the relationship between material specifications and product performance.

The main concern coming out of the conversation is engagement and role fit. Tom stated that he is increasingly interested in moving out of the day-to-day Apex work and into a role with more forward-looking development responsibility. He specifically mentioned Advanced Materials as an area he would like to explore, particularly work involving coatings, tribology, and test-method development.

Tom did not characterize this as an immediate resignation risk, but he was candid that he has felt discouraged and “stuck” since the recall announcement. He described the current work as highly reactive and said he is spending more time revisiting prior decisions than doing engineering he considers productive. He was careful not to raise a specific complaint about any individual. His comments were more generally about the volume of follow-up requests, the pace of cross-functional review, and his concern that technical input is sometimes sought after decisions have already been framed.

I recommend that Tom’s manager schedule a focused retention conversation before the end of August. The discussion should acknowledge his contributions, clarify near-term expectations, and ask directly what type of work would make the next 12–18 months sustainable for him. Given his background, a lateral move or partial assignment to Advanced Materials could be a reasonable option by Q4, subject to business need and headcount planning.

MEMORANDUM

Date: June 20, 2024
From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
Subject: End-of-Period Financial Summary - ApexHip Product Line Closure

This memorandum summarizes Finance’s current view of the ApexHip product line through June 30, 2024, including historical contribution, withdrawal-related charges, and the contingent-liability outlook. It is intended as a closing-period reference for the product line; the underlying legal and claims matters remain open.

ApexHip was launched in the United States in April 2017, following 510(k) clearance, and in Europe in September 2017. It achieved rapid adoption in its intended active-adult segment and became a material contributor to Reconstructive revenue. The line reached peak annual sales in 2020, when approximately 14,200 systems generated revenue of approximately $96 million. That represented roughly 22% of consolidated company revenue for that year.

Based on booked sales through withdrawal and remaining recognized revenue, Finance estimates cumulative ApexHip lifetime revenue of approximately $410 million for the 2017 through 2024 period. This estimate includes U.S. and international sales and is subject to routine quarter-end revenue adjustments, returns, credits, and distributor true-ups. The February 2, 2024 voluntary market withdrawal ended new commercial sales activity, although certain post-withdrawal customer credits, field inventory returns, and service-related transactions continue to be processed.

The financial impact of ApexHip has developed in stages. In the third quarter of 2022, the Company recorded an $18 million reserve for Apex-related claims. At that time, the reserve reflected known and reasonably estimable exposure, including then-pending claims activity, anticipated defense costs, and available information regarding product allegations. It did not represent a final estimate of ultimate loss.

As additional claims were filed and the federal proceeding developed, Finance’s internal range increased. During 2023 and the first half of 2024, working estimates generally placed the potential Company-funded exposure in a range of $45 million to $70 million, depending on assumptions concerning case inventory, dismissal rates, indemnity allocation, defense costs, insurance recoveries, and the timing and structure of any global resolution.

MDL 3102 currently includes approximately 520 filed cases and continues to grow. Case count alone is not a measure of ultimate liability; however, the pace of filings, claimant medical profiles, revision status, and the cost of ongoing coordinated litigation have been incorporated into our reserve analyses. Finance will continue to coordinate with Legal, Quality, Regulatory, and our outside advisors as additional case-specific information becomes available.

For planning purposes, management is evaluating a proposed settlement contribution of $80 million from Veridian, combined with a tentative $40 million coverage contribution from Aegis Specialty. These figures remain subject to negotiation, policy analysis, allocation discussions, and agreement on a mediation framework. They should not be understood as a completed settlement, a final coverage determination, or a fixed accounting conclusion. Aegis’s participation remains tentative, and any recovery will depend on finalized terms and applicable policy conditions.

The total financial effect of ApexHip therefore includes more than the product-line reserve. It also encompasses withdrawal costs, customer credits, inventory-related charges, continuing defense expense, and internal support costs. Those elements will continue to be tracked separately where practical so that reserve movements are not conflated with ordinary operational closeout expenses.

Finance will continue quarterly reserve reviews until the mediation framework is finalized and all claims are resolved. Any material change in the expected Veridian contribution, Aegis participation, case inventory, or accounting treatment will be brought forward through the standard quarter-end review process.

Owen Park
Chief Financial Officer

Attached is the current working estimate for direct costs associated with the June 14 voluntary Class II recall of ApexHip cup lots V-2200 through V-2299. This is based on the distribution file provided by Quality as of Friday afternoon: 1,140 units distributed, of which 412 are currently identified as implanted.

The estimate assumes replacement availability from unaffected inventory, return freight paid by Veridian, and reimbursement of reasonable hospital labor/handling charges for product quarantine, return processing, and replacement cases where applicable. We have included a customer goodwill credit pool for accounts with significant disruption; this has not yet been allocated by account.

| Cost Category | Basis / Assumption | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---:|
| Replacement inventory | 1,140 distributed units; transfer-cost basis for replacement cups and associated field kit utilization | $1,185,000 |
| Shipping and return logistics | Outbound replacement shipments, prepaid returns, expedited shipments for implanted-patient cases | $465,000 |
| Hospital handling fees | Quarantine, inventory reconciliation, return processing, and documented replacement-case support for 412 implanted units | $1,230,000 |
| Customer goodwill credits | Estimated credits for affected hospital accounts and distributor adjustments | $520,000 |
| Recall administration / communications | Customer notices, call-center support, effectiveness checks, and outside logistics support | $215,000 |
| Total estimated direct recall cost |  | $3,615,000 |

For planning purposes, I would carry approximately $3.4M-$3.6M pending completion of account-level reconciliation and final hospital submissions. The largest variable remains hospital handling and replacement-case reimbursement, particularly where facilities request charges beyond product handling.

This estimate is limited to the coating-related cup recall and should not be combined with the separate metal-ion/ARMD litigation exposure. Any potential claims reserve related to elevated cobalt/chromium levels, revision allegations, or other Apex product-liability matters is being tracked separately with Legal and Risk Management.

I will refresh the file once Quality completes its first effectiveness-check cycle and Sales confirms the goodwill-credit recommendations.

Manager: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Subject: Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) — Complaint Handling Specialist

Purpose

This memo documents the Performance Improvement Plan for Denise Ferro, effective August 2, 2021, developed jointly by Priya Raman and HR following performance concerns identified during preparation for the June 2021 FDA inspection of the Warsaw facility. This document is confidential and should be retained in the employee's personnel file per standard Workday HR record retention procedure.

Background

During inspection-readiness review conducted the week of June 14, 2021, Quality identified a backlog of 47 open complaints in TrackWise assigned to Ms. Ferro's queue, several of which exceeded internal timeliness targets for MDR reportability determination. Per procedure QP-0091, reportability decisions are expected within 5 business days of complaint receipt, and complaint files are expected to close within 30 days absent documented extension. Ms. Ferro's queue showed a median time-to-decision of 14 business days over the prior quarter, and multiple files remained open beyond 45 days without documented justification. This contributed to one of the three observations noted informally by the inspection team regarding complaint trending timeliness, and is a significant compliance concern given 21 CFR 803 obligations.

Performance Expectations — 60-Day Plan (August 2 – October 1, 2021)

1. Reduce open TrackWise queue from 47 to fewer than 15 complaints within the first 30 days, and to a steady-state working queue thereafter.
2. Meet the 5-business-day reportability determination target on 100% of new complaints assigned during the plan period.
3. Close 90% of complaint files within 30 days per procedure, with any exception documented and approved by Ms. Raman in advance.
4. No missed or late MDR submissions during the plan period.

Support and Check-Ins

Ms. Raman will conduct weekly one-on-one check-ins (Mondays, 30 minutes) to review queue status, discuss any files at risk of missing timeliness targets, and provide coaching. HR will participate in a check-in at the 30-day mark to assess progress. Additional TrackWise refresher training has been scheduled for the week of August 9.

Consequences

Failure to meet the metrics above by the end of the 60-day period, or any new instance of a late MDR determination during the plan period, may result in further disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment, consistent with Veridian's performance management policy.

Acknowledgment

Ms. Ferro will be asked to sign acknowledging receipt of this plan; signature does not indicate agreement with its contents, only that the plan has been reviewed and discussed.

Distribution: Denise Ferro (employee copy), Priya Raman (manager), HR personnel file

Lisa Tran
HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality

Dana, Devon:

Per procedure, I pulled the complaint population through May 10 and reconciled the event coding against the MDR log. There are 41 complaints logged since August 2018 that include elevated cobalt and/or chromium, suspected metal debris/ARMD, unexplained pain with elevated ions, or early revision with a metal-ion finding. The current working set is TW-2019-0410 through TW-2019-0451.

The cases are not evenly distributed geographically. The initial concentration is in Atlanta, principally patients from Dr. Feld’s practice; there are also several Nashville cases associated with Dr. Rao. We should be careful not to imply provider causation from that concentration. Complaint narratives contain incomplete cup-positioning information in a number of files.

On the rate analysis, the complaint rate per 1,000 implanted systems is increasing quarter over quarter from Q3 2018 through Q1 2019. I have asked Supply Chain for final lot-level distributed/implant estimates because the complaint files do not consistently contain the implant lot. I can provide the preliminary table today, with lot reconciliation to follow.

For root-cause context, Tom’s February 2019 re-analysis at 55-degree inclination appears relevant. His results showed materially higher wear under that orientation than the standard 45-degree protocol. Quality has not concluded root cause; this should be described as an evaluated design/use-condition factor alongside surgical technique, patient selection, and component factors.

Attached: Apex_MDR_Complaint_Trend_2018Q3-2019Q1.xlsx

Priya

Subject: Draft FDA recall notification - please review

Rachel,

Attached is the draft 21 CFR Part 806 recall notification package prepared for submission to CDRH regarding the voluntary recall of ApexHip acetabular cups.

Per our discussion with Bill Kowalski and Quality, the key elements summarized in the submission document are as follows:

1. Root Cause: Adhesion failure of the porous titanium KinetiCoat layer attributed to plasma-spray parameter drift following scheduled vacuum chamber maintenance at the Cork facility.
2. Scope / Lot Range: Acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured in Cork between November 2021 and February 2022.
3. Distribution Data: 1,140 total units distributed commercially; based on hospital reconciliation and registry cross-referencing to date, 412 units have been implanted.
4. Health Hazard Evaluation & Classification: Proposing a voluntary Class II classification. The risk assessment concludes that while unbonded coating flaking upon opening presents a delay in surgery or potential local inflammatory response if introduced, the probability of serious adverse health consequences remains low.

We are targeting an official submission date to the FDA district office in early June, prior to the planned formal customer notification and initiation date of June 14, 2022.

Please review the attached formal notification letter and let me know if legal has any required edits. I would appreciate your sign-off by end of day Friday, May 27, so Devon can finalize the submission packet.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Post-Market Surveillance — Interim Report

Report No.: PMS-2021-014
Date: June 28, 2021
Prepared by: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Product: ApexHip Total Hip System (all cup/head/stem configurations)
Distribution: Quality, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, Clinical Affairs (internal working file, pre-decision)

1. Purpose

This interim report summarizes post-market complaint trending for ApexHip metal-ion/wear-related events alongside external registry data from the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) and preliminary American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) figures, for the purpose of informing a cross-functional decision on next steps.

2. Complaint Trend Summary

TrackWise complaint records coded to metal-ion elevation, ARMD, pseudotumor, or related revision-for-wear categories show a sustained upward trend since 2019. Year-over-year, complaint volume in this category is up approximately 85% (2020 vs. 2019 baseline, annualized through Q1 2021 continuing the trajectory). This is not simply a function of increased implant volume — normalized against units sold, the rate per 1,000 implants is also climbing, not flat. I want to be careful here: TrackWise coding practices shifted somewhat in 2020 (see Raman's Q4 2020 coding audit), which may account for some of the apparent increase, but even a conservative adjustment leaves a real upward signal.

3. Registry Correlation

The March 2021 NJR annual report placed ApexHip's 5-year revision rate at 7.1%, against a class average (all MoM and non-MoM large-head hip systems combined) of 3.2%. That's more than double the comparator. I've cross-tabbed the NJR cohort dates against our own launch and complaint timeline and the divergence starts becoming visible in registry data roughly 3 years post-launch, which lines up reasonably well with when we'd expect edge-loading wear effects to manifest clinically if Halvorsen's 2019 high-inclination wear-test findings are operative in the field (see his Feb 2019 memo to Raman/Mendes re: 55° inclination testing, 4-6x wear vs. the 45°-only protocol used for original clearance).

AJRR data is still preliminary — we only have partial 2021 reporting — but the early read shows a similar directional trend for large-head MoM configurations generally, ApexHip included. I'd treat the AJRR numbers as corroborating rather than conclusive at this stage; sample size and reporting lag are real limitations. I'll have a fuller AJRR cut in the Q3 update.

4. Assessment

Taken together, I think we have three independent signals now pointing the same direction: internal complaint trending, NJR, and preliminary AJRR. Individually each has caveats (coding changes, single-registry limitations, immature data), but the consistency across three sources is, in my view, more than coincidental.

I'll also flag that ECO-2019-118 — the design change proposed by Halvorsen's team following the 2019 re-testing, and deferred at the time — has not been revisited since. Given the registry correlation above, I think it's reasonable to put that decision back on the table rather than treat it as closed.

5. Recommendation

I recommend the cross-functional group (Regulatory, Quality, Clinical, R&D, and Marketing) convene formally in Q3 to review this data package in full and determine whether labeling changes, a surgeon communication, or a design/manufacturing action is warranted. Given the trajectory of both the complaint data and the registry signal, I don't think this should wait until year-end review. I'm happy to present the full data set — I can also pull a more granular breakdown by cup inclination angle from surgeon-reported operative notes if that would help inform the discussion, though that will take a couple weeks to compile.

Attachments: NJR_2021_Apex_extract.xlsx, TrackWise_MoM_trend_2019-2021.xlsx

— Greg Novak
Director, Post-Market Surveillance

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
ENGINEERING MEMORANDUM

Date: March 22, 2021
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
To: KneeFlex Design History File
Subject: KneeFlex Design Change ECO-2021-044 Summary

ECO-2021-044 proposes a process change to the porous coating application used on the KneeFlex tibial baseplate. This is a manufacturing-yield change. It does not alter the finished device’s intended use, material specification, implant geometry, packaging configuration, sterilization method, or performance requirements.

1. Background and rationale

Since January, Warsaw manufacturing has seen variable yield in the tibial baseplate coating cell, primarily driven by rejects at visual inspection for incomplete coverage at the posterior edge and inconsistent surface appearance in the medial corner. The current process uses a fixed fixture angle and a single-pass application sequence. Review of batch records and line observations indicates that part orientation during the final portion of the pass is contributing to uneven deposition.

ECO-2021-044 changes the fixture orientation by 12 degrees and replaces the current single-pass sequence with two controlled passes. The proposed settings are intended to improve coverage consistency and reduce rework and scrap without changing the released coating specification. The acceptance criteria remain those currently defined in KF-WI-217 and the KneeFlex tibial baseplate drawing package.

This is not a response to a field complaint trend. There is no identified clinical or product-performance issue associated with the current process. The action is being taken to improve manufacturing yield and reduce avoidable inspection rejects.

2. Proposed verification plan

Engineering will build three pilot lots using the revised fixture and application sequence. The pilot lots will be compared against three recent production lots manufactured using the current process. Testing will include:

- Coating thickness measurements at the standard mapped locations, including posterior and medial-edge locations;
- Visual coverage inspection per KF-WI-217;
- Adhesion testing on representative coupons and baseplate samples;
- Surface roughness verification;
- Dimensional inspection of the finished baseplate after coating; and
- Review of process capability for coating thickness and visual-inspection reject rate.

The verification protocol will define sample quantities before execution. Any result outside the currently released acceptance criteria will stop implementation pending Design Assurance review. Manufacturing Engineering will also confirm that the revised fixture can be cleaned and maintained under existing work instructions.

No new clinical evaluation is proposed because the device design and coating requirements are unchanged. Regulatory Affairs will assess the completed verification package and document the basis for determining whether a new submission is required. Current assessment is that this is a manufacturing-process change within the established design envelope.

3. DHF and controlled-document updates

Before release, the following records need to be completed or revised:

- ECO-2021-044 approval record and implementation checklist;
- Updated process FMEA identifying the revised orientation and two-pass sequence;
- Revised manufacturing work instruction and fixture setup sheet;
- Verification protocol and report;
- Training records for coating-cell operators and inspectors;
- Updated process validation summary, if required by the pilot data; and
- DHF index entry linking the ECO, risk assessment, test report, and released work instructions.

The change control package should make clear that yield improvement is the reason for the change and should not characterize current production material as nonconforming unless it failed existing release criteria.

For process consistency, the change-control package follows the same template used for prior ApexHip ECOs; that reference is to document format only and does not reflect any ApexHip technical evaluation or shared design issue.

I will circulate the draft verification protocol by Friday. Manufacturing needs to reserve the coating cell for the pilot run before the April preventive-maintenance window.

Tom

For ApexHip, the reported five-year cumulative revision rate is 7.1%. The comparable class average for metal-on-metal hips in the report is 3.2%. This also appears directionally consistent with the complaint trend Priya has been tracking in TrackWise: elevated metal-ion results, pain/effusion presentations, and revisions where ARMD or adverse local tissue reaction is noted or suspected. The registry data does not establish a mechanism, and not every complaint is a confirmed device-related event, but the two data streams are corroborating each other at this point.

I recommend we convene a formal cross-functional signal review rather than continue to address this through separate PMS, complaint, and regulatory discussions. Greg

Below is the summary extract from our quarterly PMS review cross-referencing TrackWise complaint files against regional distribution figures and lot allocations through September 30, 2018.

Q3 2018 Regional Distribution & Complaint Summary (Acetabular Cups)

| Sales Region | Cup Lots Distributed | Units Implanted / Sold | Total Complaints | Complaint Rate (%) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Southeast (Atlanta focus) | V-2039, V-2041, V-2044 | 210 | 3 | 1.43% | Elevated signal (MoM/pain) |
| Northeast (Newark) | V-2015, V-2022, V-2028 | 480 | 1 | 0.21% | Nominal; surgical site infection |

| Total / Baseline Average | All Active Lots | 1,600 | 7 | 0.44% | *(Overall portfolio avg: ~0.30%)* |

Analysis & Observations

The cumulative baseline complaint rate across all commercial ApexHip acetabular lots remains stable at approximately 0.30%–0.44%. However, the Southeast cluster—specifically tied to lots V-2039, V-2041, and V-2044 shipped into the Atlanta territory—exhibits a 1.43% complaint rate (3 complaints logged against ~210 units). All three files involve early pain and reported metal sensitivity symptoms within Dr. Feld’s practice.

These three specific cup lots were produced at the Cork facility during the mid-2017 manufacturing run (June–August 2017).

At this volume, we cannot definitively separate variables. This local variance may reflect surgeon-specific placement/technique, patient selection criteria, or a subtle lot-specific material or dimensional anomaly from that production window.

Recommendation: I recommend routing these batch records to Tom Halvorsen’s engineering team for a formal technical review of lots V-2039, V-2041, and V-2044 to rule out manufacturing outliers. Quality should continue tracking regional intake in TrackWise under normal trending SOPs.

MEMORANDUM

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. — Quality Assurance

Date: August 15, 2019
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: File / Distribution per QA-SOP-014
Re: Quarterly Complaint Trending Summary — ApexHip, Q2 2019

Purpose

This memo summarizes complaint trending for the ApexHip system for Q2 2019 (April–June), per procedure QA-SOP-014 (Complaint Trending and Analysis).

Summary of Complaint Volume

A total of 11 complaints were logged in TrackWise for ApexHip during Q2 2019, up from 8 in Q1 2019. Of these, 7 complaints involved reports of elevated metal ion (Co/Cr) levels and/or early revision surgery, compared to 5 such complaints in Q1 2019. This represents a continued upward trend in metal-ion-related complaints over the last two quarters.

Complaints by region (metal-ion/revision subset, n=7):

| Region | Count |
|---|---|
| Southeast | 6 |
| Northeast | 2 |
| Midwest | 3 |

(Note: table totals to 11 as it reflects overall regional distribution for all Q2 complaints, not only the metal-ion subset; Southeast figure includes 4 metal-ion-related cases.)

Per record review, the majority of the affected implants trace to index surgeries performed in 2017–2018, consistent with prior quarters' pattern. Surgeon of record was identified in all cases; no single implanting surgeon accounts for a disproportionate share this quarter, though the Southeast region continues to represent the largest single source, consistent with Dr. Feld's practice volume in that territory.

MDR Assessment

Each complaint was individually evaluated per 21 CFR 803.50 reportability criteria. Per procedure, none of the seven metal-ion/revision complaints, taken individually, meets the threshold for mandatory reporting — none reflects a malfunction that would be likely to cause or contribute to death or serious injury if it were to recur, based on available clinical documentation at this time. Individual determinations are documented in the respective TrackWise records (TW-2019-0398 through TW-2019-0441, non-consecutive).

Trend Assessment and Recommendation

While individual complaints do not independently trigger MDR obligations, the quarter-over-quarter increase (5 to 7 in the metal-ion/revision category) is notable and, per QA-SOP-014 Section 6.2, warrants continued close monitoring going into Q3. I am recommending that this trend be flagged for consideration of a formal CAPA, given the consistency of the pattern across regions and the concentration of affected units in the 2017–2018 surgical cohort.

I also recommend coordination with Design Engineering (Tom Halvorsen) regarding the wear-testing findings at 55-degree cup inclination completed earlier this year, as several of the revision cases reference elevated inclination angles noted intraoperatively. A joint review may help clarify whether device-related factors are contributing to the observed trend, or whether this remains within expected variation for the surgical population.

This summary will be provided to Regulatory Affairs (D. Okonkwo) for awareness and to Post-Market Surveillance (G. Novak) for inclusion in the next registry data comparison.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

Executive Overview

Per Veridian SOP-QA-408 and 21 CFR 7.42, a 30-day effectiveness evaluation was conducted for the voluntary Class II recall of ApexHip acetabular cups associated with plasma-spray coating non-conformances. Initial customer notifications and consignee acknowledgment forms were dispatched commencing June 14, 2022.

Overall, 210 direct consignee accounts were identified and contacted across domestic sales territories. To date, 189 accounts have returned signed verification forms, establishing a 90.0% initial response rate. Among responding facilities, 6 affected units have been located and physically quarantined pending return authorization (RGA), and 2 units were confirmed implanted prior to notification receipt (both cases monitored; no adverse events reported). Field follow-ups remain active for the 21 pending consignees.

| Total | 210 | 189 | 90.0% | 6 | 2 | 21 |

Corrective Follow-Up

The West region currently exhibits the highest pending count (13 accounts), primarily concentrated among municipal facilities and Northgate-adjacent regional surgical centers in the Denver district. Second-notice certified mailings and local sales rep escalations have been initiated per TrackWise record TW-2022-0614. Next effectiveness audit scheduled at the 60-day mark (August 15, 2022).

Device Information

Device: ApexHip femoral head, Co/Cr

Device Operator: Dr. Marcus Feld

Complaint/Quality Record Cross-Reference: TW-2021-0938
Related Prior Complaints: No prior complaint located for patient AJ-4471 at time of initial report. Review of complaints associated with reporting surgeon remains in progress.

Event Description / Clinical Narrative

Veridian Orthopedics became aware on 02 Sep 2021 of a revision procedure performed on 19 Aug 2021 involving an ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip system. The patient reportedly presented with progressive hip pain, reduced range of motion, and elevated serum metal-ion results obtained before revision. Information provided by Atlanta Joint Institute identified serum cobalt as elevated; chromium also was reported elevated. Exact laboratory values were not available at the time of this initial report.

During revision surgery, the surgeon reported dark metallic staining and metallosis-like debris in the periarticular tissue. A pseudotumor was identified adjacent to the hip joint. The operative information further describes areas of soft-tissue necrosis. The femoral head, femoral stem, and acetabular cup were explanted and replaced with a non-metal-on-metal reconstruction.

The available clinical records characterize the indication for revision as adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), with elevated cobalt/chromium levels and local tissue findings. Veridian has not independently evaluated the explanted components or reached a conclusion regarding device causation. Operative report, pathology information, laboratory results, implant records, and explant photographs have been requested from the user facility.

Manufacturer Evaluation

Initial complaint review has been initiated under TrackWise record TW-2021-0938. The event was determined reportable as a serious injury under 21 CFR 803.50 because revision surgery was required and tissue necrosis was reported. Investigation remains open pending receipt and evaluation of additional clinical and device information.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
DESIGN ASSURANCE & PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT REPORT

DOCUMENT ID: DHF-APX-RPT-0084
REVISION: 01
DATE: March 20, 2020
TITLE: Annual Design Verification Summary – ApexHip System (2019–2020)
PREPARED BY: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, Hip Reconstruction
REVIEWED BY: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
APPROVED BY: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

1.0 PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This document provides an annual synthesis of design verification, risk management re-evaluations, and engineering change evaluations conducted for the ApexHip Total Hip System (cleared under K162447) between March 1, 2019, and February 28, 2020. The primary purpose is to ensure ongoing alignment with the Design History File (DHF), verify that changes to manufacturing processes and tooling do not adversely affect product performance, and document lifecycle verification activities pursuant to 21 CFR 820.30 and ISO 13485:2016.

2.0 SUMMARY OF DESIGN CHANGES & VERIFICATION TESTING

2.1 Packaging and Sterile Barrier Modifications
During Q2 2019, Veridian Engineering qualified an updated blister packaging seal parameter across all acetabular cup sizes (44–62 mm). Verification protocol VER-19-044 evaluated seal peel strength, dye penetration per ASTM F1929, and microbial challenge testing following accelerated aging equivalent to 5 years real-time. All acceptance criteria were met; results are logged in Agile PLM under ECO-2019-042.

2.2 Stem Broach Tooling Life Extension
In response to high utilization rates, the manufacturing team evaluated cutting efficiency and wear patterns on the Classic/Apex shared modular broach handles and broaches (sizes 1–6). Cyclic fatigue testing (3 million cycles, 2.3 kN peak load) showed no significant degradation or micro-crack initiation along the drive flats. Update released under ECO-2019-087.

2.3 Acetabular Bearing Wear Performance Characterization (Re-Analysis)
In February 2019, R&D completed an extended wear simulation re-analysis evaluating the ApexHip 36 mm and 44 mm Co/Cr head and cup articulations under non-standard, steep acetabular cup inclination angles. Initial clearance testing (Design Review DR-3, November 2016) adhered strictly to ISO 14242 standard configurations utilizing a nominal 45° inclination angle.

The supplementary simulation conducted at Meridian Testing Labs evaluated system wear at a 55° cup inclination angle to simulate potential surgical variability, component misalignment, and native anatomical variations. As documented in memo R&D-2019-014, test specimens subjected to 55° inclination exhibited dynamic edge-loading conditions that resulted in an observed 4- to 6-fold increase in volumetric wear rates compared to the 45° baseline data, alongside elevated release of cobalt and chromium metallic debris in test fluid samples.

Following cross-functional review of these findings with Quality and Product Management, an Engineering Change Order (ECO-2019-118) was proposed to evaluate cup rim geometry modifications and altered chamfer dimensions to mitigate edge-loading susceptibility. However, during the subsequent Design Review meeting, the committee voted to defer ECO-2019-118.

The rationale for deferral was documented as follows:
(a) Implementation would require extensive tooling re-qualification across the Warsaw and Cork lines, incurring substantial production disruption and tooling capital costs;
(b) Current clinical explant correlation remained limited, with confounding variables surrounding surgical technique; and
(c) The team concluded that existing surgical technique labeling adequately instructs operating surgeons regarding target cup positioning (nominally 40°–45°).

The agreed action item was to maintain the current design baseline while actively monitoring registry datasets, specifically the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) and American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR), to evaluate whether long-term clinical revision trends substantiate a physical design modification.

2.4 Distal Centralizer Injection Mold Tooling
A routine tooling replacement for the PMMA distal stem centralizers was completed in Q4 2019. Verification encompassed dimensional inspection (CMM) and dissolution testing to ensure biocompatibility and dimensional stability per print specifications (DWG-7104-B). All lots passed incoming QA inspection.

3.0 DESIGN RISK MANAGEMENT REVIEW
The ApexHip Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (dFMEA-APX-001) was reviewed. Risk priority numbers (RPNs) for head-cup subluxation and premature coating delamination were re-assessed against post-market surveillance complaint rates logged in TrackWise. While complaints regarding localized tissue reactions remain under observation, current hazard severity and probability scores remain within acceptable thresholds established under Veridian Risk Management SOP-QA-022.

4.0 CONCLUSION
Except for the deferred geometry change under ECO-2019-118, all scheduled verification activities for the period 2019–2020 have been concluded successfully. The ApexHip DHF remains active and aligned with regulatory requirements. Continued surveillance of worldwide joint registries will be maintained per PMS protocols.

MEETING MINUTES: QUALITY & REGULATORY AFFAIRS

Meeting Subject: ApexHip Complaint Trend & Wear Data Review
Date: October 4, 2019, 10:00 AM – 11:15 AM EST
Location: Warsaw HQ, Conference Room 2B / Microsoft Teams
Recorded By: Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling)

Attendees:
- Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling)
- Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs)
- Tom Halvorsen (Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip)
- Greg Novak (Director, Post-Market Surveillance)

1. Post-Market Complaint Summary (P. Raman)
- Quality reviewed the current complaint dataset logged under product code ApexHip (acetabular cup and femoral head/stem constructs).
- A cumulative total of 16 metal-ion related complaints have been entered into TrackWise since the initial cluster surfaced in August 2018 (starting with the Atlanta cases). Primary symptomology across these records includes unexplained groin pain, joint effusion, elevated serum Co/Cr levels (>7 ppb threshold), and preliminary indications of ARMD/local soft tissue reactions.
- P. Raman noted that while current complaint rates remain within broad internal threshold monitoring limits on a per-unit-shipped basis, the specific ARMD/metallosis signal shows an upward vector month-over-month.

2. Biomechanical Wear Simulation Findings (T. Halvorsen)
- T. Halvorsen presented data from his re-run of wear simulation protocols evaluating ApexHip assemblies at a 55° cup inclination angle (as opposed to standard nominal 45° alignment specified in ISO 14242 testing per the original DHF).
- Summary of findings: Testing at 55° inclination revealed micro-separation, edge-loading, and a 4× to 6× volumetric wear increase compared to baseline 45° simulation benchmarks.
- Halvorsen noted that surgeon cup placement in vivo frequently approaches or exceeds 50°–55° in routine patient anatomies, which could explain the accelerated ion release reported in the field.

3. Registry & Signal Surveillance (G. Novak)
- G. Novak provided an update on surveillance monitoring. While formal published annual registry cuts are not yet mature, preliminary AJRR hospital procedural data hints at early revision reporting for ApexHip tracking noticeably above the general category average for metal-on-poly and alternative bearing cohorts.
- Sample size remains small, but the revision trend is consistent with the track of complaints discussed.

4. Discussion & Disposition
- The group discussed immediate product actions. No consensus or decision was reached regarding halting sales or initiating field actions at this time; broader commercial and clinical leadership input would be required. The team agreed to focus on data capture, regulatory compliance, and potential engineering remediation.

Action Items
1. P. Raman: Update the TrackWise complaint intake form for total hip arthroplasty to include a dedicated, mandatory field capturing radiographic acetabular cup inclination angle where post-op films or surgical notes are obtainable. *(Target: Oct 18, 2019)*
2. D. Okonkwo: Evaluate MDR reportability obligations under 21 CFR 803 concerning aggregate complaint volume and recent trending patterns. *(Target: Oct 25, 2019)*
3. T. Halvorsen: Draft an Engineering Change Order (ECO) / design change proposal evaluating rim geometry modifications to mitigate edge-loading at steep angles. *(Target: Nov 15, 2019)*

SPEAKER NOTES / PRESENTATION OUTLINE
Presenter: Carlos Mendes, Senior Product Manager
Event: Q1 Reconstructive Sales All-Hands
Date: March 1, 2024
Deck Title: Navigating the ApexHip Transition: Field Retrospective & Portfolio Forward Look
Status: Working Draft for Slide Delivery

Slide 1: Title & Strategic Context
- Welcome everyone. I know Q1 has been exceptionally demanding across every single territory following the February 2 announcement regarding the voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip.
- The goal today is not to re-litigate the portfolio adjustments or the procedural backdrop around MDL 3102 formed back in December, but to examine how we communicated, what worked, and what must remain standardized as we shift surgeon accounts toward our core KneeFlex and revision lines.

Slide 2: Execution Under Pressure: The Withdrawal Window
- First, credit where it’s due: the overall field execution over the last four weeks has been remarkably steady under heavy fire.
- Transitioning accounts in the immediate wake of the Feb 2 notice required immense discipline. Reps were hit with aggressive clinical queries from high-volume accounts within hours.
- The majority of territories leaned heavily into the approved objection-handling deck and the verbatim FAQ sheets signed off by Legal and Regulatory. That discipline protected both the company and our individual commercial relationships.

Slide 3: Adherence to Approved Messaging vs. Field Deviation
- Let's look closely at message discipline. We rolled out the strict Apex Communication Protocol and surgeon-facing FAQ scripts in late fall 2023 specifically so no rep would feel isolated when pressed on registry numbers, revision rates, or ongoing legal proceedings.
- Where reps adhered word-for-word to the approved answers regarding clinical data, wear characteristics, and the rationale behind the withdrawal, surgeon dialogues remained professional and constructive.
- However, we did track three distinct instances in January and early February where reps freelanced:
  * One rep attempted to explain specific Co/Cr ion thresholds and biological mechanisms to a chief of surgery using non-cleared internal white papers.
  * Two reps offered speculative commentary regarding legal timelines and settlement posture during hospital coffee chats.
- In each case, we had to intervene immediately, issue formal retractions, and re-anchor the account with corporate communications. Deviation from approved messaging creates enormous exposure. Do not improvise. If it is not on the card, do not say it.

Slide 4: Recap: The Escalation Pathway
- Quick refresher on the chain established during our fall 2023 rollout:
  1. *Field Level:* Rep receives an out-of-scope question (unapproved clinical claims, specific patient ARMD symptoms, or pending litigation queries).
  2. *Regional Tier:* Escalate within 2 hours to Regional Sales Manager (Jenna Whitfield, etc.).
  3. *Commercial Lead:* RSM routes directly to me (Carlos Mendes) for product context.
  4. *Legal/RA Clearance:* Routed to Rachel Steinberg / Dana Okonkwo’s team for written response.
- This path remains active. Do not let surgeons corner you into ad-hoc debates in the scrub room. Use the bridge: *"I want to ensure you receive the definitive clinical and regulatory data on that, Dr. [Name], so let me have our Warsaw medical team provide that formal response today."*

Slide 5: Re-anchoring Account Focus
- Pivot conversation to KneeFlex and conversion strategies. Take questions.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
CORRECTIVE AND PREVENTIVE ACTION FORM

CAPA No.: CAPA-2022-0091
Title: Plasma Spray Chamber Maintenance Verification
Date Opened: 12 Jul 2022
Site/Department: Cork Manufacturing / Operations
Product: ApexHip Acetabular Cup — KinetiCoat
Related Recall: FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022
Affected Lots: V-2200 through V-2299

1. PROBLEM DESCRIPTION

Incoming inspection reports were received from Northgate Health System and a Denver hospital identifying visible flaking/delamination of KinetiCoat porous titanium coating on ApexHip cups upon removal from sterile packaging. Initial lot tracing identified cups manufactured in Cork between November 2021 and February 2022, within lots V-2200 through V-2299.

The condition presents a potential risk that coating adhesion may be inadequate for intended bone ingrowth. Distribution of affected product was stopped and the voluntary field action was initiated on 14 June 2022. A total of 1,140 units were distributed; implant status is being tracked separately through the recall file.

2. INVESTIGATION / ROOT CAUSE

Review of batch records, chamber logs, maintenance records, and retained samples identified a plasma-spray parameter drift following chamber maintenance performed in November 2021. The maintenance work included replacement and realignment of chamber components. The existing maintenance procedure required return-to-service documentation but did not require verification using a coated coupon, nor did it define acceptance criteria for confirmation of spray parameters after maintenance.

The line was returned to production based on equipment operational checks only. Subsequent review indicates that the chamber operated outside the validated parameter range for coating deposition consistency. This resulted in reduced KinetiCoat adhesion on affected cup lots.

3. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS

a. Revise WI-CORK-PS-014, “Plasma Spray Chamber Maintenance and Restart,” to require a documented maintenance verification checklist before production release.

b. Require post-maintenance coupon testing for each chamber maintenance event affecting torch, powder feed, gas flow, chamber alignment, or control settings. Coupon results must meet approved adhesion acceptance criteria before product manufacture may resume.

c. Add Quality approval to the restart checklist. Manufacturing may not release the chamber based solely on Operations sign-off.

d. Retrain Plasma Spray Operators, Maintenance, Manufacturing Engineering, and Quality personnel on the revised procedure. Training records will be maintained in the Cork training file.

4. PREVENTIVE ACTIONS

The revised checklist will be applied to both plasma-spray chambers at Cork. Maintenance work orders will include a mandatory Quality hold point. A monthly review of chamber maintenance and coupon-test records will be conducted by the Cork Quality Manager for the first six months following implementation.

5. EFFECTIVENESS CHECK PLAN

Adhesion testing will be performed on production samples from the first three post-restart lots following any qualifying maintenance event. Results will be reviewed against established specification limits and compared with pre-maintenance baseline data. No repeat coating flaking complaints, nonconforming inspection findings, or adhesion failures are acceptable during the effectiveness-check period.

Effectiveness review due: 31 Oct 2022
CAPA closure requires Quality approval.

From: Greg Novak <gnovak@veridianortho.com>
To: Priya Raman <praman@veridianortho.com>; Dana Okonkwo <dokonkwo@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2021 09:16
Subject: AJRR Q3 2021 data pull - ApexHip revision trend

Priya, Dana—

Following up on last week’s Registry Signal Review, I completed the Q3 AJRR pull using the same inclusion criteria we discussed: primary ApexHip procedures with at least 24 months of follow-up, compared with the available peer metal-on-metal cohort.

The AJRR data corroborate the direction of the March NJR findings. The absolute numbers are smaller and the confidence intervals are wider than NJR, but Apex is showing an elevated all-cause revision rate relative to peer MoM systems in the AJRR extract. The separation is most apparent in the 36–60 month follow-up band.

A few points from the stratification:

- The revision signal appears concentrated in the larger head sizes, particularly 44–50 mm. Smaller-head cases do not show the same degree of separation, although the case counts are limited.
- Where cup inclination was available in the registry record, revised Apex cases were disproportionately represented above approximately 50 degrees.
- That pattern is directionally consistent with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 high-inclination wear work. I am not suggesting the registry establishes causation; it does, however, make the edge-loading hypothesis difficult to dismiss as a laboratory-only finding.
- Revision indications remain variably coded. Pain, elevated metal ions, adverse local tissue reaction, and “other mechanical” are all present, so I would avoid relying on any single indication category without chart-level review.

I have attached the summary workbook, including the denominator definitions, exclusions, and a tab showing the inclination/head-size subset. I also included the NJR figures for reference, but did not combine the registries analytically.

Please let me know whether you want the underlying case-level list routed to Quality for complaint cross-checking. My recommendation remains that we maintain a recurring monthly review through the label-update period rather than wait for the next annual registry publication.

Greg

Date: November 8, 2022
Time: 10:00–11:15 AM ET
Location: Conference Room B / Teams hybrid
Prepared by: Devon Mitchell, Sr. Regulatory Specialist

Attendees: Dana Okonkwo (VP Regulatory Affairs), Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling), Greg Novak (Director, Post-Market Surveillance), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (Chief Medical Officer), Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel), Devon Mitchell (minutes)

Copied (did not attend): Rob Castellano (CEO)

1. Purpose
Annual refresh of the September 2021 Registry Signal Review, incorporating NJR and AJRR data through mid-2022 and current litigation posture.

2. Registry Data Update (Novak)
Greg Novak presented updated NJR figures showing ApexHip's revision rate gap versus the class average has persisted and modestly widened since the March 2021 report. AJRR figures through Q2 2022 are directionally consistent, though Novak cautioned that AJRR case volumes remain smaller and confidence intervals wider. No new signal beyond what was already flagged in 2021; the group agreed the underlying trend has not reversed.

3. Discussion — Defensibility of 2021 Decision
Dana Okonkwo opened discussion on whether the September 2021 decision to continue distribution with the labeling update and Dear Doctor letter remains defensible in light of recent developments. Rachel Steinberg noted that outside counsel (Whitfield & Barr) has received inquiries from plaintiff-side counsel that suggest state-court filings are being prepared, and that the company should anticipate the first suits could be filed as early as Q1 2023. Steinberg advised the group to document the clinical and regulatory rationale contemporaneously rather than reconstruct it later.

4. Clinical Perspective (Adeyemi)
Dr. Adeyemi reiterated his view, consistent with the 2021 review, that individual patient risk-benefit analysis still favors continued availability for most candidates, particularly lower-BMI patients with appropriate cup positioning, but acknowledged the registry gap is now a longer trend rather than a single data point. He stated he is not currently recommending withdrawal on clinical grounds alone but agreed the totality of registry, complaint, and now anticipated litigation signals warrants continued monthly monitoring rather than annual-only review.

5. Action Items
- Novak to refresh registry trend charts quarterly going forward rather than annually, circulate to Okonkwo/Raman/Mitchell.
- Mitchell to update the internal signal-tracking log with today's data points and attach to the DHF-adjacent regulatory file.
- Okonkwo/Raman/Steinberg to prepare a combined board briefing summarizing (a) the registry trend, (b) current reserve status per Finance, and (c) litigation posture, for presentation ahead of year-end; target circulation to Castellano by early December.
- Steinberg to keep the group apprised of any confirmed filings.

6. Next Meeting
To be scheduled following completion of the board briefing materials, or sooner if a filing is confirmed.

RE: Formal Complaint – ApexHip System Early Revision (Patient Ref: RM-7104)

Dear Ms. Raman:

I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding a catastrophic failure of the ApexHip total hip system in a 54-year-old male patient whom I revised last week, exactly 38 months post-index procedure.

The patient presented with severe groin pain, persistent clicking, and joint effusion. Workup revealed markedly elevated metal ions, with serum cobalt measured at 18.7 ppb (chromium was 12.4 ppb). Intraoperatively, upon arthrotomy, I encountered profound metallosis with extensive soft tissue necrosis surrounding the abductor mechanism and a large pseudotumor extending anteriorly. The acetabular cup (54 mm) and femoral head (44 mm) showed obvious eccentric wear bands. The components were stable at the bone interface, but the local tissue destruction was severe enough to require extensive debridement and conversion to a constrained revision construct.

I specifically reviewed the initial postoperative films; cup inclination was 51 degrees, which is well within acceptable clinical placement for active patients. In speaking informally with several regional colleagues over the summer, I understand I am not the only surgeon seeing this pattern. Is Veridian tracking other reports of ARMD and accelerated wear with the ApexHip? Specifically, has your engineering team identified a design issue or edge-loading vulnerability with this cup at higher inclination angles?

Given the severity of the tissue destruction I observed, I expect a prompt and detailed written response regarding whether this event is being investigated under your CAPA system and reported to regulatory authorities. The explanted components have been decontaminated and retained per protocol.

Sincerely,

James Whitaker, MD
Denver Orthopedic Specialists
Attending Orthopedic Surgeon
