Re: Important Product Information — ApexHip Total Hip System — Updated Labeling Regarding Revision Rate Data and Recommended Patient Monitoring

Dear Doctor,

This letter is being sent to surgeons who use, or have used, the ApexHip Total Hip System to provide you with updated safety information regarding revision rates observed in orthopedic joint registries and to communicate an update to the product's Instructions for Use (IFU).

In March 2021, the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) published its annual report, which included five-year revision data for ApexHip. The NJR figures indicate a 5-year all-cause revision rate of 7.1% for ApexHip, compared to a class average of 3.2% for metal-on-metal total hip systems reported in the same registry period. Veridian Orthopedics has reviewed this data alongside internal post-market surveillance information and continues to evaluate revision trends through our post-market surveillance program.

After careful review, Veridian has determined that ApexHip will remain available for use, with an updated IFU that reflects this registry information and provides additional guidance to support patient management. The updated IFU is enclosed with this letter and is also available through your Veridian sales representative or by contacting our Regulatory Affairs department directly.

We recommend that surgeons consider the following with respect to patients who have received an ApexHip implant:

1. Enhanced clinical follow-up, including assessment for symptoms consistent with adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), such as groin or hip pain, swelling, or noise from the joint.
2. Consideration of serum cobalt and chromium ion level testing in symptomatic patients, and as clinically indicated in asymptomatic patients based on your clinical judgment.
3. Consideration of cross-sectional imaging (e.g., MARS MRI or ultrasound) where ARMD is suspected, per your institution's standard practice.
4. Continued reporting of any adverse events or revisions associated with ApexHip to Veridian's Complaint Handling department and, where applicable, to appropriate national registries.

We take this matter seriously and are committed to ongoing monitoring of ApexHip performance through registry data, complaint trending, and post-market clinical follow-up. Additional questions regarding this notification may be directed to the undersigned or to your Veridian regional sales representative.

Thank you for your continued partnership and your attention to your patients' care.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

Subject: Draft 483 Response — Observation 1, ApexHip Complaint Trending

Dana / Devon,

Attached (Apex_483_ObsResponse_Obs1_draft1.docx) is my first pass at the response language for Observation 1 from the June 2021 Warsaw inspection (Investigator Delgado). Per procedure, I'm circulating for your review before we finalize with legal input, since Observation 1 goes directly to the timeliness of our complaint trending process for ApexHip.

Summary of proposed corrective actions:

1. Revised Complaint Trending SOP (QA-SOP-0447, rev. D). We are updating the SOP to require documented monthly trend calculation for ApexHip revision-related complaints, rather than the quarterly cadence currently in place. This addresses the inspector's finding that trend review intervals did not support timely signal detection.

2. Monthly Management Review. Effective August 2021, ApexHip revision-related complaint trends will be reviewed monthly by a cross-functional group (Quality, Regulatory, PMS, and Clinical) rather than folded into the general quarterly complaint review. Minutes will be retained in TrackWise as supporting documentation.

3. Post-Market Surveillance Strengthening / Registry Signal Review. As part of the broader effort to strengthen our post-market surveillance posture for ApexHip, I want to explicitly reference in the corrective action section the Registry Signal Review meeting currently planned for September 2021, which will incorporate the NJR five-year revision data alongside our internal complaint trend. I think tying the monthly review commitment to that meeting gives the response more teeth and shows FDA we're not treating trending as a paperwork exercise.

For context/support in the response narrative, I'm citing the same trend figures I sent over last month: ApexHip revision-related complaints per TrackWise increased from 22 in Q1 2020 to 38 in Q1 2021. That's the number the investigator was looking at when he raised the timeliness concern, so I think we need to own it directly in the response rather than try to soften it — better to show we caught the trend and are acting on it.

Devon, can you check the CFR citations in section 3 (I have 21 CFR 820.100 and 820.198 referenced, want to make sure I'm not missing a cross-reference to the MDR reporting piece)? Dana, let me know if you want the Registry Signal Review reference pulled back — I know that meeting hasn't happened yet and I don't want us committing to an outcome in writing before it occurs, just to the fact that trending data will feed into it.

Target for FDA submission is still July 21 per the 15-business-day response window.

Priya

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REVIEW

Employee: Greg Novak
Title: Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Review Period: January 1, 2021 – December 31, 2021
Review Date: February 8, 2022
Manager: Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
HR Business Partner: Lisa Tran
Overall Rating: Strong Performer

Performance Summary

Greg delivered a strong year in a role that required both technical rigor and sound judgment under difficult circumstances. He maintained the post-market surveillance reporting calendar, improved the readability of registry analyses for non-clinical stakeholders, and was a dependable partner to Quality, Clinical, and Regulatory Affairs.

Of particular note, Greg’s work on the March 2021 NJR annual report was thorough and appropriately escalated. His analysis identified that ApexHip’s five-year revision rate was reported at 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. Greg did not overstate what the registry could establish, but he was clear that the signal warranted further review alongside complaint data, available literature, and subsequent AJRR information. His NJR/AJRR analyses were well organized, traceable to source data, and useful in helping leadership understand the difference between a signal, a trend, and a clinical conclusion.

Greg also handled a difficult presentation to senior leadership professionally. The discussion involved challenging questions regarding whether the observed registry performance could be explained by patient mix, surgeon learning curve, implant positioning, or other factors. Greg remained measured, answered within the available data, and identified the limitations rather than trying to resolve them with assumptions. Dr. Adeyemi specifically noted Greg’s preparation and composure during this process.

Key Contributions

• Produced clear NJR and AJRR surveillance summaries and maintained supporting source files.
• Escalated the March NJR finding promptly through the established PMS process.
• Supported cross-functional review of ApexHip revision and complaint information.
• Improved recurring surveillance materials by using consistent rate comparisons and plain-language conclusions.
• Continued to support routine surveillance obligations despite increased volume and scrutiny.

Development Priorities

Greg’s primary development goal for 2022 is cross-functional communication, particularly with Regulatory Affairs. Greg’s analysis is rigorous, but Regulatory sometimes needs earlier notice when a draft conclusion may affect MDR assessment, external correspondence, labeling, or planned communications. The goal is not to dilute the analytical discussion; it is to establish clearer timing, ownership, and documentation of handoffs between PMS, Quality, Clinical, and RA.

Suggested actions include a standing monthly review with Dana Okonkwo’s team, advance circulation of draft registry summaries where feasible, and a documented escalation path for potential new signals. Greg should also continue tailoring presentations for executive audiences while preserving the underlying analytical detail.

Overall Assessment and Recommendation

Greg is a strong performer whose work materially supported informed decision-making during a challenging year. He is viewed as a valued technical leader with important institutional knowledge in registry surveillance and comparative revision-rate analysis. I recommend Greg be considered for retention bonus treatment in the 2022 cycle, subject to the applicable program criteria and leadership approval.

Lisa Tran
HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality

Following consultation with outside counsel (Whitfield & Barr), our independent actuarial advisors, and formal review by the Audit Committee during yesterday afternoon's executive session, finance has finalized the accrual methodology for product liability exposure associated with the ApexHip system.

Pursuant to ASC 450-20 (*Loss Contingencies*), we have determined that an adverse outcome across pending and anticipated claims is probable and reasonably estimable. Effective for the close of Q3 2022, Veridian Orthopedics will book a pre-tax product liability reserve of $18.0 million. This adjustment will be reflected in our upcoming Form 10-Q filing within accrued liabilities and detailed in Note 8 (*Commitments and Contingencies*).

Reserve Composition and Actuarial Basis

The $18.0 million figure represents the low-to-midpoint estimate derived from outside actuarial modeling across two distinct tranches of exposure:

| Exposure Category | Basis / Patient Population | Estimated Reserve |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Tranche A: Coating Adhesion Claims (Recall Z-1418-2022) | Direct remediation, surgical costs, and indemnity related to 412 implanted units from affected cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 (Cork plasma-spray drift). | $4.2M |
| Tranche B: MoM Wear / ARMD Claims (Registry Signal & Wear Profile) | Projected 3-year claim emergence based on NJR/AJRR 5-year cumulative revision divergence (7.1% vs. 3.2% benchmark) and anticipated multi-district coordination. | $13.8M |
| Total Accrued Reserve | | $18.0M |

Tranche A modeling specifically isolates the 412 documented implantations originating from the 1,140 distributed cups recalled on June 14, 2022. Tranche B accounts for the broader systemic risk driven by adverse tissue reaction/ARMD reports, factoring in the filing cadence anticipated by W&B as plaintiffs' firms consolidate filings following the September 2021 registry signal disclosures.

Insurance Coverage and Carrier Notification

Notice of Circumstance was formally submitted to our primary product liability carrier, Aegis Specialty Insurance, on July 19, 2022. Rachel’s team remains in dialogue with their coverage counsel. As anticipated given the dual-track nature of the manufacturing defect versus long-term biological response claims, Aegis has indicated they will issue a formal Reservation of Rights letter before month-end. Consequently, no insurance recovery receivables have been recognized as an offset against this accrual under GAAP matching principles.

Hannah is adjusting the Q3 consensus bridge and operational forecast models accordingly. Please direct any specific questions regarding footnote wording to Rachel and myself ahead of the external auditor sign-off next week.

Internal Memorandum

Date: February 11, 2019
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
To: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Subject: ApexHip wear re-test results at 55 degree inclination

Priya, Carlos —

Wanted to get this in front of you before I go any further with it, because I don't love what I'm seeing.

Back at DR-3 in 2016 we locked the wear-test protocol at 45 degrees inclination only, per ISO 14242, and that's what's been in the DHF ever since. I've been sitting on a hunch since last fall that we should be checking off-nominal cup positioning too, since that's closer to what actually happens in a lot of real hips depending on surgical technique. So I had Meridian Labs re-run the protocol at 55 degrees cup inclination on a fresh set of cup/head pairs, same lot family as production, same head material (Co/Cr on Co/Cr).

Results are in — Meridian report MTL-19-0142, dated 2/6/19. Raw numbers:

- 45° inclination (standard, matches our cleared data): ~2.1 mm3 per million cycles volumetric wear, consistent with what we submitted in the 510(k).
- 55° inclination: ~9.8–12.4 mm3 per million cycles, depending on the sample. That's 4 to 6x higher than standard angle.

This is not subtle. The wear scar pattern on the cup rim at 55° is exactly the edge-loading signature I flagged in my concept-phase notes back in 2015 when we were still finalizing head/cup clearance tolerances — I'd predicted this could happen at high inclination but we didn't build it into the formal test matrix because ISO 14242 doesn't require it and DR-3 decided standard angle was sufficient for clearance purposes. In hindsight I think that was the wrong call, or at least an incomplete one.

I know this is a MoM system, so wear debris isn't just a mechanical problem — it's a Co/Cr ion generation problem, and higher wear volume at higher inclination is going to mean higher ion release in patients who end up with cups sitting steep, whether that's from surgical variability or from cup design geometry not tolerating it well.

Priya — has TrackWise flagged anything that could line up with this? I'm thinking about the Atlanta cluster from last August, three patients out of Feld's practice. I don't have visibility into implant positioning on those cases but if any of them were high-inclination placements this could be more than coincidence.

I want to be careful here — this is one lab run, small sample, and I haven't done the statistics properly yet (need to look at variance across the sample set before I say anything definitive). But the magnitude is big enough that I think we need to start looking seriously at either a design change to cup geometry (bigger clearance angle tolerance, maybe a modified rim profile) or reconsidering head material/size combinations to reduce edge-loading sensitivity.

Can we get 20 minutes this week to talk through next steps? I'd rather we get ahead of this than have it come up some other way.

Tom

Dear Orthopedic Surgeon:

Veridian Orthopedics remains committed to patient safety and post-market clinical monitoring. We are writing to provide important post-market surveillance updates regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System.

Recent data published in the National Joint Registry (NJR) annual report noted a 5-year cumulative revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip construct, compared to a contemporary class average of 3.2% across metal-on-metal systems. While Veridian continues to support the overall safety profile and functional performance of the ApexHip system in appropriately indicated active patients, our internal technical evaluations indicate that acetabular cup orientation is critical to long-term wear characteristics.

Specifically, we strongly recommend that operating surgeons pay meticulous attention to the cup inclination angle during implantation, targeting an abduction angle within 40° to 45° to minimize edge-loading. We are currently implementing enhanced surgical guidance and updating our product labeling to support optimal placement technique.

TO: File (Workday Case Ref: INV-2021-089)
FROM: Lisa Tran, HR Business Partner – R&D and Quality
DATE: January 20, 2022
SUBJECT: Hotline Investigation Summary – Report H-2021-047

1. BACKGROUND & SCOPE
On November 18, 2021, an anonymous report was submitted via the Veridian Ethics Hotline (Ref # H-2021-047) alleging that personnel within the Quality and Complaint Handling department were deliberately suppressing adverse event complaint trending related to the ApexHip system. Specifically, the reporter alleged that metal-on-metal wear and metallosis/ARMD complaint rates were intentionally slow-walked or reclassified in TrackWise to avoid triggering premature internal regulatory escalation and external mandatory reporting.

Human Resources initiated a formal internal inquiry in coordination with the Legal department. Over the past seven weeks, investigative interviews were conducted with seven current employees across Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and Regulatory Affairs, including Complaint Handling Specialists, Post-Market Analysts, and department leadership. A review of relevant TrackWise escalation workflows, standard operating procedures (SOP-QA-402, SOP-RA-110), and internal correspondence was also performed.

2. INVESTIGATION FINDINGS
Based on the totality of interview statements and contemporaneous records, the investigation concludes that there is no substantiated evidence of intentional or malicious suppression of complaint data or adverse event trending by Quality leadership or individual complaint specialists.

However, the inquiry identified material process vulnerabilities and cross-functional communication breakdowns:
* Documentation Gaps: Escalation discussions between Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling) and Dana Okonkwo’s Regulatory Affairs team frequently occurred via informal verbal touchpoints or ad hoc check-ins rather than structured, formal TrackWise or Agile escalation records. This lack of formal audit-trail documentation gave junior team members the perception that concerns were being dismissed or stalled.
* Procedural Ambiguity: While individual adverse event MDR determinations adhered strictly to 21 CFR 803 decision trees per procedure, thresholds for aggregate "out-of-trend" statistical escalations were inconsistently understood between the primary complaint handlers and post-market surveillance.

3. RECOMMENDATIONS & OUTCOMES
1. Managerial Coaching: HR will implement targeted leadership and communication coaching for Priya Raman. Coaching will focus on transparent downward communication, structured upward handoffs, and reinforcing psychological safety within her reporting chain so team members do not feel compelled to seek anonymous escalation channels.
2. Process Alignment & Training: Quality and Regulatory Affairs must jointly update the interface SOP governing complaint trending escalations. Mandatory retraining will be assigned in Workday Learning for all Quality complaint-handling staff before end of Q1 2022.
3. Legal Coordination: In light of anticipated litigation exposure regarding ApexHip performance and registry data, this investigation summary and associated interview memoranda have been shared with Elena Ruiz at Whitfield & Barr LLP.

This matter is considered closed from an internal HR workplace conduct standpoint, pending execution of the corrective coaching and process actions noted above.

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs), Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (Chief Medical Officer), Marcus Lee (VP, Sales)
FROM: Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)
DATE: September 28, 2021
SUBJECT: Draft "Dear Doctor" Letter – ApexHip Acetabular System Labeling Update

Following the decisions reached during our September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I have prepared the initial draft text for the upcoming customer notification ("Dear Doctor" letter) regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System.

As agreed by the review team and executive leadership, Veridian will maintain active commercial distribution of ApexHip while implementing an immediate Instructions for Use (IFU) labeling update to address emerging registry trends.

Background & Signal Summary
The primary driver for this communication is data presented from the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report, which identified a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip construct, compared to an average class benchmark of approximately 3.2% across contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) hip resurfacing and total replacement systems. While internal clinical evaluations indicate that well-positioned constructs continue to demonstrate strong clinical survivorship, registry data and internal engineering assessments correlate early revisions predominantly with adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) linked to elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels.

Proposed Letter Content & Labeling Guidance
The draft notification emphasizes patient safety, precise surgical technique, and targeted post-operative vigilance:

1. Patient Monitoring Recommendations: We advise clinicians to establish heightened routine clinical and radiographic follow-up protocols for all implanted ApexHip patients, with particular attention to individuals receiving larger femoral head diameters (≥44 mm). Routine cross-sectional imaging (MARS-MRI or ultrasound) and periodic blood metal-ion quantification (whole blood cobalt and chromium) should be considered annually or upon any presentation of unexplained pain, clicking, or swelling.
2. Surgical Positioning & Angle Inclination: Revisions strongly correlate with edge-loading phenomena. The revised labeling explicitly instructs surgeons to target an acetabular cup inclination angle within 40° to 45° and anteversion between 15° and 20°. Operating outside these ranges—specifically exceeding 50° of operative abduction—markedly increases the risk of accelerated fluid-film wear and premature component loosening.

Next Steps & Timeline
Our target mail date to all US and EU implanting orthopedic surgeons, chief medical officers, and relevant risk management personnel is mid-October 2021. Reps will receive accompanying talking points once this text is locked.

Please review the attached formal notification layout (`Apex_Dear_Doctor_Draft_v1.docx`) and provide your redlines. We require formal sign-off from Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Clinical before Dana submits the final package to the agency and we proceed with mass distribution.

MEMORANDUM

TO: ApexHip Design History File (DHF-0042)
FROM: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, Reconstructive R&D
DATE: March 22, 2019
SUBJECT: Design Change Evaluation – ECO-2019-118 (Acetabular Cup Sub-Hemispherical Geometry Modification) – DEFERRED STATUS
CC: Priya Raman, Director of Quality; Carlos Mendes, Product Manager; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

1. Purpose
This memorandum documents the technical review, simulator wear-testing results, and final disposition rationale for Engineering Change Order ECO-2019-118 regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System. Under 21 CFR 820.30(i), this record captures the engineering evaluation and formal decision to defer the proposed design modification.

2. Background and Proposed Change
ECO-2019-118 was initiated in January 2019 to evaluate potential cup modifications intended to reduce edge-loading phenomena under steep cup placement. The proposed change comprised a 1.2 mm reduction in cup coverage angle and an increased rim blend radius across sizes 44–62 mm to broaden the functional safe zone during micro-separation and steep operative inclination.

3. Simulator Wear-Testing Summary
Initial pre-market clearance wear testing was conducted by Meridian Testing Labs in 2016 per ISO 14242-1 standard parameters (45° inclination angle, 1.0–2.0 mm head offset). Under this standard protocol, the ApexHip system demonstrated low volumetric wear rates compatible with cleared predicate performance:
* Report MT-2016-0882: *ISO 14242-1 ApexHip 45° Wear Simulator 5.0 Mc Cycle Testing* (Meridian Testing Labs, final report dated November 14, 2016). Mean steady-state wear rate: 0.82 mm³/Mc.

In February 2019, R&D contracted supplemental simulator wear testing at an elevated inclination angle of 55° to assess wear kinetics under non-ideal surgical alignment and extreme biomechanical positioning:
* Report MT-2019-0144: *ApexHip Kinematic Wear Characterization at Steep Inclination (55°)* (Meridian Testing Labs, final report dated February 18, 2019).

The 55° protocol demonstrated a pronounced escalation in metallic wear, showing a 4× to 6× increase in volumetric wear rate (mean steady-state wear rate: 4.65 mm³/Mc) compared to the standard 45° setup. Gravimetric analysis and laser surface profilometry confirmed that steep orientation induces localized contact stress spikes along the superior rim, resulting in edge-loading and rim stripe wear.

4. Rationale for Deferral
On March 8, 2019, an engineering and product cross-functional review convened to evaluate ECO-2019-118. The decision was reached to defer implementation based on the following considerations:

1. Limited Clinical Correlation: ISO 14242-1 at 45° remains the recognized consensus standard for total hip replacement testing. Elevated angles (55°) represent severe boundary conditions that exceed typical surgical alignment targets (Lewinnek safe zone: 40° ± 10°). At present, post-market surveillance data (TrackWise) does not show a verified in vivo correlation between the steep bench simulation and active customer complaint trends.
2. Requalification and Re-clearing Burden: Tooling re-qualification across the full shell matrix (sizes 44–62 mm), updated validation runs at Cork, and potential 510(k) supplementary filings would involve significant resource allocation and lead times (estimated 12–16 months), which is not warranted absent a confirmed clinical failure mechanism.
3. Surveillance Strategy: Rather than redesigning the implant geometry based on extreme simulator parameters, the team determined that post-market monitoring is the appropriate risk control. R&D and Quality will actively track domestic and international arthroplasty registry data, specifically monitoring revision signals from the National Joint Registry (NJR) of England and Wales and the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR).

5. Conclusion and Review Cycle
ECO-2019-118 is formally placed in DEFERRED status in Agile PLM. This design change evaluation will be revisited annually during management review or immediately upon identification of a confirmed clinical or registry signal indicating adverse wear performance in the field.

Tom Halvorsen
Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

INTERNAL MEMORANDUM

Date: January 20, 2021
From: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
To: File / Distribution — Sales Leadership, Marketing, Customer Operations
Subject: ClassicHip Discontinuation Announcement Plan

Purpose

This memo outlines the communication plan for the formal discontinuation of ClassicHip, effective per the phase-out schedule approved by the Reconstructive leadership team. The goal is a clean, professional off-ramp that protects customer relationships and positions ApexHip as the natural upgrade path for surgeons and facilities currently on ClassicHip.

Key Dates

- Final order acceptance: June 30, 2021. All ClassicHip purchase orders must be received by this date; no exceptions without VP Sales sign-off.
- Last shipments: December 2021. Remaining finished-goods inventory in Warsaw will be allocated against outstanding orders and shipped out by year-end.
- Internal systems (Salesforce product catalog, price lists) to reflect ClassicHip as "legacy — discontinuing" starting February 1, 2021, and "discontinued" after July 1.

Distributor and GPO Communication

Customer Operations, working with Legal, will issue formal discontinuation notification letters to all active ClassicHip distributors by February 15, 2021. These letters will confirm the final order date, expected last-ship window, and point of contact for transition questions. In parallel, we need to begin GPO contract amendment discussions — VantageOne and our other national accounts will need updated addenda removing ClassicHip SKUs and, where applicable, adding ApexHip at existing or renegotiated pricing tiers. I'd like Owen's team looped in early given the revenue-neutral intent of these amendments.

Surgeon Transition Support

For active ClassicHip surgeons, Jenna's and the other regional teams should proactively schedule one-on-one transition conversations rather than waiting for surgeons to notice the SKU disappearing from ordering portals. We should offer:

- Case observation/proctoring support for surgeons moving to ApexHip who haven't used it before
- Instrument tray familiarization sessions
- A short leave-behind comparing ClassicHip and ApexHip sizing ranges so OR staff aren't caught off guard mid-case

For surgeons who prefer to move to a competitor system rather than adopt ApexHip, reps should handle that gracefully — no pressure tactics, and no disparagement of competitor products. The objective is a good exit, not a forced conversion.

Positioning ApexHip as the Recommended Alternative

Where surgeons are undecided, the sales team should lead with ApexHip's practical upgrade story: the broader head diameter range (36–50mm versus ClassicHip's more limited offering) gives surgeons more intraoperative flexibility for stability and range of motion, and the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating offers a modern bone ingrowth surface compared to ClassicHip's older fixation approach. This is a pure product-transition talking point — think of it as "here's what's newer and more capable," not a commentary on ClassicHip's performance. Marketing will prepare a one-page comparison sheet along these lines for rep use by mid-February.

Next Steps

Anika's team will draft the distributor letter language and comparison sheet this week. I'll circulate a review draft to Sales, Legal, and Customer Operations by January 29 for comment before the February 15 mailing deadline.

Carlos

DESIGN REVIEW MINUTES: ECO-2019-118

Meeting Date: March 11, 2019
Time: 1:30 PM – 2:55 PM EST
Location: Warsaw HQ (The Hub) – Conference Room 3B / WebEx
Chair: Tom Halvorsen (Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip)
Attendees:
- Tom Halvorsen (Sr. Design Engineer)
- Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling)
- Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)
- Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs)

1. Wear Testing Re-Analysis & Proposed Rim Modification
T. Halvorsen reviewed findings from the February 2019 wear-simulator re-run conducted at a 55° cup inclination angle (evaluating steep abduction). Simulator data demonstrated a 4–6× increase in volumetric wear rates relative to the baseline 45° ISO 14242 testing used for the original DHF and clearance. The proposed ECO-2019-118 introduces a modified acetabular cup rim geometry—specifically increasing the peripheral edge chamfer and modifying the sub-hemispherical relief radius—to reduce edge loading and rim impingement under elevated abduction angles.

2. Commercial, Cost, and Tooling Discussion
C. Mendes and T. Halvorsen presented initial financial projections for implementing the modification across all cup sizes (44–62 mm). Estimated non-recurring engineering and execution costs total approximately $1.2M, including:
- Re-tooling and CNC fixture rework at manufacturing sites: ~$650k
- Requalification wear testing at Meridian Testing Labs (multi-station simulators, 5 million cycles): ~$350k
- Packaging and manufacturing line changeover validation: ~$200k

Mendes raised commercial concerns regarding justifying a $1.2M expenditure and product change while clinical market feedback remains overwhelmingly positive and adoption is accelerating. It was emphasized that real-world registry evidence remains sparse given the limited duration the product has been on the market (launched US April 2017).

3. Regulatory and Quality Considerations
D. Okonkwo addressed regulatory requirements under 21 CFR 807.81(a)(3). Okonkwo advised that because ApexHip’s substantial equivalence rationale under K162447 directly relied on predicate bearing geometry and existing wear characteristics, altering the articular contact area and rim dimensions could significantly affect safety and effectiveness. This would likely require a new 510(k) submission rather than a internal Letter-to-File. A new 510(k) would entail an estimated 6–9 month review timeline, substantial internal documentation overhead, and potential commercial disruption.

P. Raman noted that while three metal-ion complaints were logged in TrackWise out of Atlanta in late 2018, overall complaint trending across commercial volume does not currently indicate a systemic field failure.

4. Conclusion & Disposition
The review committee concluded that immediate execution of ECO-2019-118 is premature based on available clinical performance data balanced against tooling, requalification costs, and regulatory impact.

Decision: Defer implementation of ECO-2019-118. The design modification will remain on hold pending receipt and evaluation of broader longitudinal registry and complaint data. The committee will formally revisit the ECO if post-market complaint rates or registry revisions show negative trending.

Action Items
1. Greg Novak (Post-Market Surveillance): Closely monitor upcoming registry releases, specifically tracking UK National Joint Registry (NJR) and AJRR data sets for any emerging signal regarding ApexHip revision rates. *(Due: Ongoing / Q2 2019 Review)*
2. Tom Halvorsen (R&D): Archive 55° simulator wear reports and maintain ECO-2019-118 package in Agile under "Deferred" status. *(Due: March 22, 2019)*
3. Priya Raman (Quality): Track commercial complaints in TrackWise under code ARMD/metal wear to flag any volume clusters. *(Due: Monthly PMS Review)*

REGISTRY SIGNAL REVIEW
Agenda
Tuesday, September 14, 2021 | 9:00–10:00 AM
The Hub — Reserve B

Prepared by: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
Attendees: Dana Okonkwo, Priya Raman, Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Carlos Mendes, Marcus Lee

Purpose: Review the current registry signal for ApexHip and align on whether continued commercialization with risk-mitigation measures remains appropriate, or whether a voluntary market withdrawal should be considered.

1. NJR annual report — March 2021
   • Review ApexHip five-year revision rate: 7.1% versus 3.2% class average.
   • Review available stratification by age, head size, and revision indication.
   • Discuss limitations of registry comparators and signal persistence.

2. AJRR data update
   • Review late-2021 AJRR extracts and preliminary trend analysis.
   • Compare directionality with NJR findings, including early revisions associated with elevated metal ions, ARMD, and unexplained pain where reported.
   • Confirm data completeness and planned refresh cadence.

3. Clinical risk assessment
   • Dr. Adeyemi to present clinical interpretation of the registry findings, including potential patient consequences of delayed revision and appropriate surveillance considerations.
   • Discuss whether current labeling adequately addresses cup-positioning, metal-ion monitoring, and patient selection.

4. Commercial/regulatory options

RE: Urgent Quality and Safety Notification / Formal Product Complaint
ApexHip System: Recalled Inventory (Lot V-2247) and Unrelated Early Revisions

Dear Ms. Raman:

I am writing to formally log serious concerns regarding your ApexHip system. First, regarding the recent voluntary Class II recall notice we received dated June 14, 2022, my hospital's central sterile and incoming inspection team quarantined several components earlier this week. Specifically, an Apex acetabular cup from lot V-2247 showed visible coating delamination inside the sterile blister pack prior to presentation in the OR. The KinetiCoat porous surface was actively flaking off in small particulate fragments when the inner packaging was inspected.

This is unassisted flaking on unwrapping, which is completely unacceptable for an implant intended for immediate press-fit biological fixation. We have returned six unopened units from this lot to our local distributor per your recall instructions, but I demand an explicit accounting of what happened with your plasma-spray process and how this passed lot release.

Beyond this manufacturing recall, however, I must formally document two severe clinical failures involving ApexHip components implanted well prior to the recalled lot run. Both appear directly related to metal-on-metal wear and adverse local tissue reactions:

1. Patient D.K. (DOB 11/14/1963): Primary left total hip performed March 2019 (Cup Lot V-1892, 54mm; Head Lot H-3112, 44mm). Patient presented at 38 months post-op with groin pain and severe functional decline. Pre-op serum cobalt was 9.4 ppb; chromium was 8.1 ppb. During revision on June 18, 2022, I observed extensive metallosis, fluid-filled cystic collections, and abductor necrosis consistent with ARMD. The cup was well-fixed, but significant edge-wear was obvious on the bearing surface.

2. Patient R.M. (DOB 04/02/1958): Primary right total hip performed August 2018 (Cup Lot V-1644, 52mm; Head Lot H-3088, 40mm). Revised on June 27, 2022. The patient exhibited a 6 cm pseudotumor displacing the femoral neurovascular bundle. Explant revealed gross blackened fluid and extensive soft tissue destruction. Tissue samples confirmed severe histiocytic response and metal debris necrosis.

Both explant sets have been retained in formalin per standard hospital protocol and are available for your engineering team to analyze. Please provide immediate TrackWise reference numbers for these adverse events and confirm receipt of this correspondence.

Sincerely,

James M. Whitaker, MD
Mile High Orthopedic Specialists
Attending Orthopedic Surgeon, Denver Presbyterian Hospital

EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE / POST-MARKET SURVEILLANCE REVIEW

MEETING MINUTES: REGISTRY SIGNAL REVIEW (APEXHIP)

Date: September 14, 2021
Time: 10:00 AM – 11:45 AM EST
Location: Executive Boardroom (Warsaw HQ) / Microsoft Teams Video Conference
Recording Secretary: Devon Mitchell (Sr. Regulatory Specialist)

ATTENDEES
* Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
* Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
* Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
* Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
* Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
* Marcus Lee, VP Sales, Reconstructive
* Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
* Devon Mitchell, Sr. Regulatory Specialist (Minutes)

1. CALL TO ORDER & PURPOSE
The meeting was convened at 10:02 AM by D. Okonkwo to evaluate cumulative post-market surveillance data regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System, specifically focusing on comparative registry performance trends identified in the United Kingdom National Joint Registry (NJR) 2021 Annual Report and preliminary datasets from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR).

2. PRESENTATION OF REGISTRY DATA (G. NOVAK)
G. Novak presented an analysis of international and domestic joint registries through Q2 2021:
* NJR Data (UK): The ApexHip system demonstrates an estimated cumulative revision rate of 7.1% at five years post-implantation across all sizes. By comparison, the broader metal-on-metal (MoM) and hybrid total hip arthroplasty class benchmarks at an average 3.2% revision rate at the same interval.
* AJRR Data (US): US registry signal indicators parallel the NJR trend, showing an upward trajectory in revision risk specifically associated with larger diameter femoral head constructs (≥44 mm) and higher acetabular component abduction/inclination angles (>45°).
* Observed Failure Modes: The primary indications cited for revision within the registry cohorts include pain of unexplained origin, adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD) / pseudotumor formation, and aseptic loosening.

3. CLINICAL RISK-BENEFIT ASSESSMENT (DR. L. ADEYEMI)
Dr. L. Adeyemi provided clinical context regarding the registry findings:
* The observed delta in revision rates is clinically relevant; however, the clinical benefit of high-demand stability, low dislocation rates, and reduced mechanical wear in younger, highly active patient populations remains viable when the implant is positioned strictly within the target Lewinnek safe zone (inclination ≤45°).
* The primary driver of accelerated metal-ion release and secondary local tissue reactions appears clinically correlated with surgical placement techniques (edge-loading at steep inclination angles) rather than an intrinsic systemic design flaw across all patient demographics.
* Dr. Adeyemi concluded that immediate market withdrawal is not clinically warranted at this juncture, provided that operative instructions and risks regarding component positioning are communicated with heightened clarity to operating surgeons.

4. DISCUSSION & REGULATORY DETERMINATION
The committee reviewed potential courses of action: voluntary market withdrawal versus commercial continuation accompanied by targeted risk mitigation (labeling modifications and formal clinician notification).

* M. Lee and C. Mendes emphasized that commercial partners and clinical key opinion leaders require immediate guidance to prevent misinterpretation of NJR data in the field, noting the commercial disruption of a full withdrawal without definitive surgical positioning guidance.
* D. Okonkwo and P. Raman advised that regulatory standards permit commercial continuation under a controlled risk mitigation strategy, provided that the FDA is notified of significant labeling updates and that complaint trending under 21 CFR 820.198 continues with increased surveillance frequency.
* Decision: Following consensus discussion, the committee determined to continue global distribution and sales of the ApexHip system, contingent upon an expedited labeling update highlighting cup inclination limitations and the issuance of an urgent clinician notification letter ("Dear Doctor" letter).
* Executive Concurrence: R. Castellano confirmed executive agreement with the recommended approach, noting that surgeon education and precise placement parameters represent the appropriate, measured path forward.

5. ACTION ITEMS

|:---|:---|:---|
| 1. Draft formal 510(k) labeling update submission emphasizing strict acetabular cup inclination tolerances (target ≤45°) and enhanced warnings regarding metal-on-metal adverse reactions. | D. Okonkwo | October 1, 2021 |
| 2. Draft comprehensive "Dear Doctor" communication outlining registry observations, proper patient selection, and intraoperative positioning precautions for surgeon distribution. | C. Mendes / Dr. L. Adeyemi | September 28, 2021 |
| 3. Establish bi-weekly complaint trending protocols and explant analysis monitoring within TrackWise for all incoming ApexHip metal-ion and revision reports. | P. Raman | September 21, 2021 |
| 4. Maintain ongoing data reconciliation with AJRR working groups to track domestic revision velocity. | G. Novak | November 15, 2021 |

6. ADJOURNMENT
The meeting was formally adjourned at 11:45 AM.

Devon Mitchell, Sr. Regulatory Specialist

As we prep the field for potential questions ahead of any customer-facing communications on the cup lot matter, I want to make sure everyone is drawing a clean line between two separate topics. We've seen some blending of these in call notes and I want to nip that before it becomes a pattern.

Two distinct issues — keep them separate

Coating/lot issue (Cork manufacturing) — a limited number of acetabular cup lots (V-2200 through V-2299, produced Nov 2021–Feb 2022) showed a coating adhesion irregularity identified during incoming inspection at two facilities. Don't

MEMORANDUM

To: Sarah Kim, Mike Ruiz
From: Jenna Whitfield, Regional Sales Manager, Southeast
Date: October 12, 2021
Subject: Talking points: if a surgeon asks about the Dear Doctor letter

Team—

A few of you have already gotten questions after the Dear Doctor letter went out, especially from offices that follow the registry data closely. I want us to be consistent, straightforward, and not get pulled into trying to practice medicine from the field.

If a surgeon asks, the opening should be simple:

> “Veridian issued the letter to make sure surgeons have the updated labeling information and can consider it in their own clinical judgment. ApexHip remains cleared and available for use.”

Do not characterize the letter as “just administrative,” “nothing,” or “a non-issue.” It is a labeling update, and the fact that we are communicating it directly is intentional. We can say that the updated materials include additional information regarding patient selection, follow-up, and factors that may affect implant performance. Please use the approved leave-behind and make sure the office has the current IFU.

If the conversation turns to revision rates or metal ions, acknowledge the question rather than arguing with the surgeon. Something along these lines works:

> “I understand why you are asking. Registry information is one input among several, and Veridian has updated the labeling so surgeons can evaluate the current information alongside their own patient population and experience.”

What we should not say:
- “Those revisions are all from bad technique.”
- “The registry numbers are wrong.”
- “Nobody needs to worry about metal ions.”
- “This will not happen with your patients.”
- Anything that sounds like a guarantee, including “Apex will last longer” or “your revision rate will be lower.”

We also should not promise a clinical outcome, a particular cobalt/chromium level, or that a patient will not require revision. That is not our lane, and it creates a problem for everyone.

For detailed questions about the NJR data, comparative revision rates, patient monitoring, metal-ion testing, or a specific clinical scenario, please route the surgeon to Medical Affairs. Send me the surgeon’s name, institution, and the question asked, and I will coordinate with Carlos and Dr. Adeyemi’s team. If it is time-sensitive, call or text me rather than trying to answer from memory.

Sarah, please be particularly careful with Atlanta accounts. Mike, same for any Nashville follow-up from Dr. Rao’s network. These are sophisticated surgeons; they will know when someone is reading a script. Be candid, stay within the approved message, and listen more than you talk.

Thanks,

Jenna Whitfield
Regional Sales Manager, Southeast
Veridian Orthopedics

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2021 09:16
Subject: AJRR Q3 2021 data pull - ApexHip revision trend

Priya, Dana—

Following up on last week’s Registry Signal Review, I completed the Q3 AJRR pull using the same inclusion criteria we discussed: primary ApexHip procedures with at least 24 months of follow-up, compared with the available peer metal-on-metal cohort.

The AJRR data corroborate the direction of the March NJR findings. The absolute numbers are smaller and the confidence intervals are wider than NJR, but Apex is showing an elevated all-cause revision rate relative to peer MoM systems in the AJRR extract. The separation is most apparent in the 36–60 month follow-up band.

A few points from the stratification:

- The revision signal appears concentrated in the larger head sizes, particularly 44–50 mm. Smaller-head cases do not show the same degree of separation, although the case counts are limited.
- Where cup inclination was available in the registry record, revised Apex cases were disproportionately represented above approximately 50 degrees.
- That pattern is directionally consistent with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 high-inclination wear work. I am not suggesting the registry establishes causation; it does, however, make the edge-loading hypothesis difficult to dismiss as a laboratory-only finding.
- Revision indications remain variably coded. Pain, elevated metal ions, adverse local tissue reaction, and “other mechanical” are all present, so I would avoid relying on any single indication category without chart-level review.

I have attached the summary workbook, including the denominator definitions, exclusions, and a tab showing the inclination/head-size subset. I also included the NJR figures for reference, but did not combine the registries analytically.

Please let me know whether you want the underlying case-level list routed to Quality for complaint cross-checking. My recommendation remains that we maintain a recurring monthly review through the label-update period rather than wait for the next annual registry publication.

Greg

To: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel

From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer

Date: August 5, 2022

Subject: Q3 2022 Apex Litigation Reserve — Draft Memo

Attached is the current draft for the Q3 close materials. I am circulating this now because the proposed reserve is material enough that I do not want the first substantive discussion to occur in the audit committee pre-read.

We are proposing an $18.0 million reserve for ApexHip-related claims and associated costs in Q3 2022. The working allocation is as follows:

| Component | Proposed Reserve | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Anticipated product-liability / litigation exposure | $11.0M | Filed and threatened patient claims, counsel assessment, complaint trend, revision signal |
| Recall-related warranty and replacement costs | $7.0M | V-2200–V-2299 field action, replacement product, credits, hospital handling and related service costs |
| Total | $18.0M |  |

The $11.0M litigation component remains an estimate rather than a case-specific accrual schedule. We have a relatively small number of asserted claims today, but the underlying indicators are moving in the wrong direction. In particular, the March 2021 NJR reporting showed a five-year Apex revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. The later registry information has not provided a basis to dismiss that signal. TrackWise complaint counts also continue to rise, including complaints involving elevated Co/Cr levels, pain, suspected ARMD, and early revision.

The $7.0M recall component is limited to the June field action for cup lots V-2200 through V-2299. That estimate includes expected replacement and credit exposure for distributed product, hospital administrative costs where contractually required, return processing, and an allowance for additional warranty requests. It does not assume that the coating issue and the metal-ion allegations share a common cause. For accounting purposes, however, both items are Apex-related and need to be visible together in the Q3 discussion.

Hannah: please run the variance cases against the current FY22 forecast and provide (1) the Q3 P&L effect, (2) cash timing through Q4 2023, and (3) the revenue sensitivity if accounts defer Apex purchases following the recall notice. I would also like a base, downside, and severe-case view rather than a single-point estimate.

Rachel: please review the proposed contingency language, especially the distinction between known recall costs and estimated exposure from asserted or anticipated claims. I do not want us to overstate certainty where the claims landscape is still developing, but the committee will reasonably ask why the reserve is increasing now.

Rob: absent a significant change in the underlying numbers, my recommendation is that we book the full $18.0M in Q3 and discuss it with the audit committee as a discrete Apex matter rather than burying it in the broader warranty line.

Please send comments by noon Monday so we can finalize the pre-read package.

Owen

From: Greg Novak
To: Dana Okonkwo; Priya Raman
Date: Thu, 16 Jun 2022 09:47
Subject: Registry data post-recall - any change in ApexHip revision trend?

Dana, Priya,

Following up two days out from the recall announcement. Wanted to flag something before it gets asked at a higher level.

The V-2200–V-2299 recall is a coating adhesion issue traced to plasma-spray drift at Cork — mechanically it's unrelated to the revision-rate signal we've been tracking out of NJR (7.1% at 5 years vs. 3.2% class average) and the AJRR data. That signal is driven by edge-loading wear and elevated Co/Cr, not coating flaking at inspection. Different failure mode, different population — the recalled lots weren't even implanted long enough to be in the 5-year registry cohort.

That said, I'd bet money plaintiffs' counsel will try to blur the two, and honestly some surgeons will too once they hear "recall" and "ApexHip" in the same sentence. Dr. Whitaker in Denver already conflates every Apex complaint into one bucket.

I think it'd be smart to get ahead of this with a short internal FAQ that clearly separates the coating issue from the metal-ion/revision-rate issue, in plain language, in case the board or comms needs to respond to press or surgeon questions. I can draft a first pass on the registry side if Priya can cover the complaint-handling angle and Dana can sanity-check the regulatory framing.

Let me know if this makes sense to prioritize this week.

Greg

To: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
From: Meridian Testing Labs
Subject: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report - ApexHip Prototype Lot P-001

Report No.: MTL-16-4478
Protocol: MTL-WEAR-14242-16 Rev. B
Test Article: ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip prototype assemblies, Lot P-001

1. PURPOSE

At Veridian Orthopedics’ request, Meridian Testing Labs performed wear simulation testing on ApexHip prototype total hip assemblies to evaluate bearing wear under the conditions defined in ISO 14242. Testing was conducted in accordance with the approved protocol, MTL-WEAR-14242-16 Rev. B, dated 18 November 2016.

2. TEST ARTICLES AND SETUP

Five ApexHip prototype assemblies from Lot P-001 were received on 21 November 2016. Each assembly consisted of a cobalt-chromium femoral head and matching cobalt-chromium acetabular cup. The cup specimens included the KinetiCoat porous titanium exterior coating; coating performance was not evaluated as part of this wear test.

Assemblies were mounted in the multi-station hip simulator using a nominal cup inclination angle of 45 degrees. The simulator applied the ISO 14242 gait loading and motion profile in bovine serum lubricant, diluted to the protein concentration specified by the protocol. One loaded control assembly was maintained under soak conditions for correction of fluid uptake.

Testing was run to five million cycles, with gravimetric measurements obtained at one-million-cycle intervals. Component surfaces were visually inspected at each interval for gross damage, discoloration, or abnormal wear patterning.

3. RESULTS

The mean calculated volumetric wear rate for the four test assemblies was 2.1 mm3 per million cycles. Individual specimen results ranged from 1.8 to 2.4 mm3 per million cycles. No specimen demonstrated a progressive increase in wear rate over the test duration.

| Measurement | ApexHip Prototype Lot P-001 | ClassicHip Predicate Reference* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean volumetric wear rate | 2.1 mm3/million cycles | 5.8 mm3/million cycles |
| Range | 1.8–2.4 mm3/million cycles | 4.9–6.7 mm3/million cycles |
| Test duration | 5 million cycles | 5 million cycles |

*Predicate reference values supplied by Veridian from its ClassicHip wear-performance file.

Visual inspection identified light, uniform polishing of the bearing surfaces consistent with simulator operation. There was no gross scratching, deformation, fracture, or evidence of abnormal material loss observed under the tested conditions.

4. SCOPE LIMITATIONS

All testing was conducted at the standard 45-degree cup inclination angle specified in the approved protocol. No testing was performed at elevated or reduced inclination angles, under edge-loading conditions, or under deliberately malpositioned assembly conditions. Accordingly, this report does not characterize wear performance outside the tested 45-degree configuration.

5. CONCLUSION

ApexHip prototype units from Lot P-001 demonstrated a mean wear rate of 2.1 mm3 per million cycles during ISO 14242 simulation testing. This result is within the wear-performance target provided by Veridian and compares favorably with the ClassicHip predicate reference values. Based on the testing performed, the ApexHip design meets wear performance targets under the tested conditions.

Prepared by:
Meridian Testing Labs
Wear Simulation Laboratory

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS
QUALITY ASSURANCE & REGULATORY COMPLIANCE
MEMORANDUM

TO: Complaint Investigation File (TrackWise)
FROM: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
DATE: September 10, 2018
SUBJECT: MDR Reportability Assessment – TW-2018-0311, TW-2018-0322, TW-2018-0340
CC: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Devon Mitchell, Sr. Regulatory Specialist

1. Purpose & Scope
This memorandum documents the Medical Device Reporting (MDR) reportability determination per internal procedure SOP-QA-404 (*Adverse Event Reporting and MDR Decision Trees*) and 21 CFR 803.50 for three recent complaint files originating from Dr. Marcus Feld’s clinical practice (Atlanta Joint Institute). All three cases involve the Veridian ApexHip Acetabular Cup system paired with Co/Cr modular heads.

2. File Assessments

A. TrackWise Record: TW-2018-0322
* Device Identification: ApexHip Cup, 52 mm (Lot V-2041); ApexHip Femoral Head, 40 mm (Lot H-3118). Implanted October 2017.
* Clinical Presentation: Patient presented at 10 months post-op with persistent groin pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion. Serum cobalt levels measured at 11.4 µg/L; chromium at 8.2 µg/L. Aspiration and MARS MRI revealed extensive local fluid collection and soft tissue inflammation consistent with metallosis. Dr. Feld has scheduled a revision surgery for October 4, 2018 to explant the acetabular and femoral bearing components.
* MDR Determination: REPORTABLE. Under 21 CFR 803.50(a)(1), this event constitutes a reportable serious injury. The event necessitated surgical intervention (revision arthroplasty) to preclude permanent impairment of a body structure/function resulting from local tissue reaction and adverse local tissue response (ALTR).

B. TrackWise Record: TW-2018-0340
* Device Identification: ApexHip Cup, 56 mm (Lot V-2044); ApexHip Femoral Head, 44 mm (Lot H-3142). Implanted December 2017.
* Clinical Presentation: Patient reported severe pain and gait instability at 8 months. Whole blood cobalt was confirmed at 14.1 µg/L. Ultrasound-guided aspiration recovered turbid, dark-stained synovial fluid indicative of metal debris. Operative notes from Dr. Feld recommend urgent revision due to progressive tissue necrosis and pseudotumor formation.
* MDR Determination: REPORTABLE. In accordance with 21 CFR 803.50, this case satisfies the criteria for serious injury requiring medical/surgical intervention to prevent irreversible tissue damage.

C. TrackWise Record: TW-2018-0311
* Device Identification: ApexHip Cup, 50 mm (Lot V-2039); ApexHip Femoral Head, 38 mm (Lot H-3094). Implanted September 2017.
* Clinical Presentation: Initial complaint indicated mild trochanteric bursitis and an initial cobalt draw of 6.2 µg/L. Radiographs demonstrate well-fixed components with no observable osteolysis or pseudotumor. Revision has not been recommended; the patient is undergoing physical therapy.
* MDR Determination: NON-REPORTABLE AT THIS TIME (HELD PENDING DATA). The current clinical presentation does not meet the serious injury threshold under 21 CFR 803.3. File is held pending secondary laboratory cobalt retest data and clinical follow-up records from the clinic, expected by September 24, 2018.

3. Action Items
1. Quality has updated the MDR disposition blocks in TrackWise for TW-2018-0322 and TW-2018-0340 to "Reportable."
2. Recommend Devon Mitchell prepare draft initial FDA Form 3500A submissions for lots V-2041 and V-2044 to ensure timely submission within the 30-day statutory clock.
3. Post-Market Surveillance will maintain active monitoring on TW-2018-0311 (Lot V-2039) pending retest panels.

Owen,

Per our discussion, I refreshed the Apex model using September actuals and the current field forecast. The model is intended to frame revenue exposure through FY24; it does not attempt to estimate claim severity or timing.

Apex FY22 is now expected to close at approximately $71.0M, versus the $96.0M peak in FY20. The decline began before the June cup recall in the underlying order data. The more pronounced step-down follows the September 2021 labeling update and what Sales characterizes as increased surgeon caution after the NJR data circulated. The recall remains a separate, lot-specific assumption in the model, although several field teams report customers are not making that distinction.

Summary output ($M):

| Scenario | FY22E | FY23E | FY24E | FY22–FY24 Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Status quo / current label | 71.0 | 62.4 | 60.1 | (15%) |
| Label-driven decline | 71.0 | 54.7 | 45.9 | (35%) |
| Full market withdrawal | 71.0 | 48.3 | 42.6 | (40%) |

The status quo case assumes current labeling remains in place, no broad commercial action, and modest attrition offset by existing account utilization. It is the closest to the current Sales operating plan, though I would not characterize it as the base case with high confidence.

The label-driven decline case assumes continued loss of new implanters, lower utilization among accounts that have moved Apex to a limited-use position, and increasing price concessions where distributors seek to retain volume. This case reflects the present trajectory in the Southeast and selected Midwest accounts more closely than the operating plan.

The withdrawal case assumes no new commercial placements after an orderly market action, with only limited residual revenue from contracted inventory and replacement requirements. This is necessarily a planning construct, not a recommendation regarding product status.

For reserve adequacy testing, I recommend using the full withdrawal scenario as the conservative revenue sensitivity. It produces the lowest contribution available to absorb claims-related costs and avoids relying on a recovery in surgeon confidence that we are not seeing in the current forecast submissions.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEETING MINUTES

Meeting: Registry Signal Review
Date: September 14, 2021
Time: 3:00–3:45 p.m.
Location: Reserve B, Warsaw HQ
Prepared by: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

Attendees: Rob Castellano, Priya Raman, Greg Novak, M.D., Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Carlos Mendes, Rachel Steinberg, Dana Okonkwo

Purpose
To review the ApexHip registry signal and determine whether the appropriate action is continued commercial distribution with risk communication/labeling changes or a market withdrawal.

Discussion

1. Registry data. Mr. Novak summarized the March 2021 UK National Joint Registry annual report and subsequent internal review. At five years, ApexHip’s reported revision rate is 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average for comparable total hip systems. The differential remains material after accounting for the relatively younger, more active patient population in the Apex cohort. Preliminary AJRR extracts reviewed in August are directionally consistent, though the U.S. data are less mature and have wider confidence intervals.

2. Complaint and clinical review. Ms. Raman confirmed that complaint handling and MDR assessments remain active under established procedures. The complaint profile includes elevated cobalt/chromium laboratory values, pain, and revisions in a subset of patients. Not every revision has an identified ARMD finding, and available explant and operative information is inconsistent. Quality will continue trending under 21 CFR 820 requirements and assess reportability under 21 CFR 803 on an event-specific basis.

3. Design history. The group reviewed the February 2019 re-analysis performed by Mr. Halvorsen’s engineering team. Testing at 55-degree cup inclination, rather than the standard 45-degree protocol used in the original verification work, showed approximately four- to six-fold increased wear under edge-loading conditions. The proposed design change was not implemented at that time. The finding supports a potential mechanism for increased metal debris in malpositioned or high-inclination implants but does not establish that all observed revisions are attributable to the device.

4. Clinical assessment. Dr. Adeyemi stated that ARMD is a known risk of metal-on-metal hip systems and, based on the current record, is manageable through more explicit surgeon communication, patient selection, follow-up, and earlier evaluation of symptomatic patients. He recommended a Dear Doctor letter addressing cup positioning, metal-ion evaluation where clinically indicated, and monitoring of patients with pain or other concerning symptoms. He did not recommend an immediate market withdrawal at this time.

Decision

Following discussion, the group agreed to continue selling ApexHip while implementing a labeling update and Dear Doctor communication. Mr. Castellano approved this plan. Regulatory Affairs will coordinate review of revised labeling and the surgeon letter; Quality and PMS will continue complaint and registry surveillance; Marketing will ensure all field materials are aligned with the approved communication.

Ms. Steinberg noted that litigation exposure associated with the revision-rate signal, complaint history, and continued sales should be assessed. She requested that relevant analyses and decision materials be preserved and not forwarded outside the working group without Legal review.

The potential financial reserve associated with ApexHip claims was raised but not resolved during this meeting. Mr. Castellano requested a separate follow-up with Owen Park to review the available information and appropriate next steps.

Action Items

- Okonkwo/Mitchell: circulate draft labeling update and Dear Doctor letter for review by September 21.
- Adeyemi: provide clinical language and monitoring recommendations for the letter.
- Novak: update registry analysis upon receipt of the next AJRR extract.
- Raman: continue complaint trending and provide a monthly summary to the group.
- Steinberg/Castellano/Park: schedule follow-up regarding potential financial exposure and reserve considerations.

Dana

MEMORANDUM

Date: April 10, 2024
From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
Subject: Q2 2024 Reserve and Funding Scenario Memo — ApexHip Mediation Fund

This memo lays out three funding scenarios for the potential ApexHip mediation settlement fund that Rachel has flagged as a likely outcome of the MDL 3102 mediation track, currently estimated in the $60M–$100M range. I want to get this in front of the audit committee before we close Q2, so treat this as a discussion draft, not a final recommendation.

Scenario 1: Fully self-funded via reserve increase.
We book the full estimated exposure as an increase to the existing $18M Apex reserve. At the low end ($60M) this is roughly a $42M incremental charge; at the high end ($100M) it's about $82M incremental. Hannah's team ran this through the model and depending on where in the range we land, this hits diluted EPS by an estimated $0.85 to $1.40 per share for the year. That's a big swing and I don't love it as a base case — it also assumes zero offset from Aegis, which I think is too conservative given where the coverage dispute stands.

Scenario 2: Partial Aegis coverage.
If the aggregate limit dispute with Aegis resolves in our favor — meaning they don't succeed in treating all the recall and MDL claims as a single occurrence under one limit — we could see up to $50M in coverage applied against the settlement fund. This meaningfully changes the EPS picture, cutting the range roughly in half depending on settlement size. The open question is timing and certainty: outside coverage counsel hasn't given us a firm opinion yet on how the aggregation language in the policy will be read, and Rachel's team is pushing them for that. I'd treat this as our base case for planning purposes, but I want to flag clearly that it is contingent on a legal opinion we don't have in hand yet.

Scenario 3: Hybrid — partial reserve, partial debt facility.
A blended approach where we fund some portion through the reserve and draw on a mid-2024 debt facility for the balance, smoothing the EPS hit over a longer period and preserving some liquidity flexibility. This is probably our fallback if the Aegis dispute drags past Q2 or resolves against us, but I haven't had time to model covenant impacts yet and want more runway before we present numbers on this one.

Recommendation.
My recommendation is that we plan around Scenario 2 as the working base case, with Scenario 1 as the downside case we disclose sensitivity around, and Scenario 3 held in reserve as a contingency if the coverage picture doesn't clarify in time. I want to stress this is provisional — we should not finalize any of this without input from outside coverage counsel on the Aegis aggregate limit question, and I think this whole analysis needs to go in front of the audit committee before we lock the Q2 close numbers, given the materiality here.

I'd like to get 30 minutes with Rachel, Hannah, and me before the next audit committee prep session to align on messaging. Let's take the covenant modeling for Scenario 3 offline for now — not ready for a broader audience yet.

Owen

Subject: Engineering Status Review: ECO-2019-118 (Apex Acetabular Cup Rim Geometry & Clearance) — Closing the Loop

MEMORANDUM

TO: Priya Raman, Director of Quality & Complaint Handling; Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
FROM: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
DATE: January 10, 2022
SUBJECT: Engineering Status Review: ECO-2019-118 (Apex Acetabular Cup Rim Geometry & Clearance) — Closing the Loop

I am writing to formally revisit the open engineering posture surrounding ECO-2019-118. It has now been nearly three years since I submitted the initial Engineering Change Order proposal in February 2019, and our Design History File (DHF) index still does not accurately capture where we stand on this.

To recap the technical history: during the development phase leading up to Design Review 3 (DR-3) in November 2016, our wear simulator protocol was established strictly under ISO 14242-1 standard parameters, testing acetabular component placement at a nominal 45° inclination angle only. The Meridian Testing Labs reports confirmed acceptable volumetric wear under those ideal, nominal conditions, which supported our 510(k) clearance (K162447). However, as I flagged in my February 2019 re-analysis memo, testing the system under steeper acetabular cup inclinations—specifically 55°—produced severe edge-loading dynamics. The wear simulator data showed a 4× to 6× increase in gravimetric and volumetric metal wear rates compared to the 45° baseline, driven by localized contact stresses at the cup rim during microseparation cycles.

ECO-2019-118 proposed an immediate modification to the acetabular rim radius and polar clearance profile to mitigate edge-loading wear at non-ideal cup angles (which clinical data shows occur frequently in real-world patient anatomy).

In mid-2019, leadership decided to formally defer ECO-2019-118. The stated rationale at the time centered on commercial friction: tooling changeout costs, scrap write-downs, and especially the timeline required for full mechanical and simulator requalification, which would have disrupted peak production volumes.

Here is my primary concern today: as of January 2022, three full years after we identified the 4–6× wear multiplier under steep angles, no design change has been implemented. None. The product currently being shipped from Warsaw and Cork retains the exact rim geometry cleared in 2017.

Furthermore, I reviewed the ApexHip DHF index in Agile last week and noticed ECO-2019-118 is marked as "Closed / Superseded by Commercial Labeling Review." This is factually incorrect and creates an audit vulnerability. The engineering risk was never resolved or designed out; it was *deferred*. We should not be relying solely on post-market technique guides or surgeon education to manage a mechanical wear condition that we know occurs once the cup tilts past 50°.

I recommend two immediate corrective actions:
1. Re-open the DHF index entry for ECO-2019-118 and formally designate its status as "Deferred — Pending Clinical Registry / Post-Market Review," explicitly noting that the original ISO 14242 protocol tested only 45° inclination and did not evaluate edge-loading conditions.
2. Reconvene the cross-functional engineering review team (Quality, Product Management, R&D) to decide whether we are going to requalify the modified rim tooling or leave the deferred status on the permanent record.

We have known about the edge-loading wear multiplier since early 2019. Leaving the change order in administrative limbo without a clear engineering resolution is a significant unaddressed risk.

Regards,

Tom Halvorsen
Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

From: Lisa Tran, HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality
Subject: Performance Improvement Plan Closure - Complaint Handling Specialist
Employee: Denise Ortiz, Complaint Handling Specialist, Quality & Complaint Handling
Manager: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

This memorandum documents the conclusion of Denise Ortiz’s 90-day Performance Improvement Plan (“PIP”), effective October 4, 2022.

Denise was placed on a PIP on July 5, 2022, following recurring missed MDR triage deadlines and an accumulated TrackWise intake backlog. The concern was not the quality of Denise’s clinical documentation when completed, but timeliness in completing initial complaint assessment, escalation, and routing steps under the Complaint Handling procedure. During the review preceding the PIP, Denise’s on-time triage rate was 62%, with several items requiring reassignment or manager follow-up before the applicable MDR decision window could be confirmed.

The PIP established the following expectations:

1. Complete initial triage and routing of assigned complaint records within the procedural timeframe, absent documented clinical or customer follow-up needs.
2. Maintain an on-time triage rate of at least 85% for the review period.
3. Review the open TrackWise queue with Priya Raman twice weekly and identify items requiring support before deadlines lapse.
4. Escalate potential MDR-reportable events promptly and document the rationale for any pending determination.
5. Participate in refresher training on complaint intake, MDR decision trees, and queue-management practices.

Denise completed the required refresher training on July 12, 2022. She also adopted a daily priority review and used the twice-weekly queue meetings to flag records awaiting operative notes, product identification, or clinical follow-up.

Performance during the PIP review period was as follows:

| Review Period | Assigned TrackWise Records | Triaged On Time | On-Time Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pre-PIP baseline | 87 | 54 | 62% |
| July 5–August 4 | 46 | 38 | 83% |
| August 5–September 4 | 51 | 45 | 88% |
| September 5–October 3 | 47 | 43 | 91% |

Across the 90-day period, Denise closed or timely triaged 126 of 144 assigned TrackWise records. The remaining records were documented as pending external information or reassigned pursuant to the escalation process; none were permitted to lapse without manager visibility. Priya has confirmed that Denise’s recent work has been more consistent, that potential MDR matters are being surfaced earlier, and that the prior backlog associated with Denise’s queue has been substantially resolved.

Based on the foregoing, HR and management recommend that Denise’s PIP be closed successfully effective October 4, 2022. Denise is expected to sustain the performance improvements described above and continue to follow established complaint-handling and MDR triage procedures.

Priya will conduct a follow-up performance check-in with Denise in approximately 90 days, during the first week of January 2023. HR will remain available to support that discussion and will retain this memorandum and related PIP documentation in Denise’s confidential personnel file.

Lisa Tran
HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality
